title: Dell delivers record results, but Wall Street sees a catch
summary: Dell's AI business is booming, and a new $25 billion buyback signals confidence.
content: Dell Technologies delivered another record quarter, raised its annual forecasts and authorized billions in additional share buybacks. Yet Wall Street initially reacted by selling the stock. Reuters reported Wednesday, Nov. 25, that Dell Technologies (DELL) shares fell 5.7% in early trading despite the company’s stronger outlook and an additional $25 billion share repurchase authorization. The stock later recovered, closing 0.6% higher at $297.06. The erratic response followed the exceptional profits report. Driven by the increasing demand for AI servers, Dell’s fiscal third-quarter sales more than doubled to a record $54.9 billion. Additionally, the corporation revised its full-year sales prediction higher for the third time this year, from $192 billion to $202 billion. Reuters reported Tuesday that the new forecast exceeded analysts’ expectations of approximately $194.5 billion. However, the market’s initial reaction reflected growing apprehension about the massive expenditures required to sustain AI growth. Investors are becoming more skeptical of technology firms’ ability to turn their infrastructure investments into long-term earnings. For Dell shareholders, the tension is striking: The company is reporting record demand, but investors still want convincing evidence that the growth can last. Dell’s AI server business delivers record results Dell’s most recent financial results show how drastically AI has changed the company’s operations. For the fiscal third quarter, the firm posted adjusted profits of $9.45 per share, which was higher than analysts’ projections of $6.59 and up 265% from the same period last year. Dell’s Infrastructure Solutions Group generated $42 billion in revenue, representing a 198% annual increase, according to its Nov. 24 earnings release. The company’s major financial highlights included: Total revenue: $54.9 billion, up 103%. AI server revenue: $22 billion, up 291%. Traditional server and networking revenue: $15 billion, up 235%. Storage revenue: $4.9 billion, up 24%. Adjusted earnings per share: $9.45, up 265%. AI server backlog: $132.3 billion. Dell received $60.2 billion in AI server orders in the quarter, indicating continued computing infrastructure growth. Jeff Clarke, COO, said the company evaluates orders based on customer quality, financing capacity, and infrastructure. The large backlog gives Dell visibility into future demand, but orders must be fulfilled and revenue generated. Why Wall Street remains cautious about Dell Dell’s earnings come amid growing skepticism about the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending. Reuters reported Wednesday that technology stocks faced renewed pressure as investors questioned the financing behind large data center expansions. These worries have impacted businesses that provide servers, processors, and other equipment. In addition, growing memory prices and concerns about future profitability put pressure on Dell. The company’s infrastructure operating margin reached 17%, up from 12.4% a year earlier, although investors remain concerned about the outlook for hardware margins. Another issue is Dell’s conventional PC business. Although operating income fell by 6%, its Client Solutions Group’s sales increased by 3% to $12.9 billion. Dell’s quarterly figures show that consumer PC sales dropped 15% to around $1.6 billion. The disparity shows how much business infrastructure investment, as opposed to regular PC customers, now drives Dell’s growth. Dell makes a bold $25 billion bet as investors hesitate Bloomberg / Getty Images Dell’s $25 billion buyback sends a different message Dell’s management is expressing confidence in the company’s financial prospects, despite the market’s initial pessimism. The board expanded its current buyback program by approving an extra $25 billion in share repurchases. Dell also returned a record $4.9 billion to shareholders through dividends and repurchases during the quarter. Dell has not yet acquired $25 billion worth of shares as a result of the expanded authorization. Over time, it increases management’s ability to buy back shares. Although the financial advantages depend on purchase price and execution, buybacks may reduce the number of outstanding shares and perhaps increase per-share profits. Although the permission is a positive signal for investors, the dangers associated with future AI expenditure remain. What Dell’s latest forecast means for shareholders Dell now expects fiscal 2027 AI server revenue of $78 billion, up from its previous $74 billion forecast. The company also raised its adjusted annual earnings outlook to $29.68 per share from $25.50. Fourth-quarter revenue is projected to reach approximately $56.3 billion, with adjusted earnings of $8.40 per share. These numbers imply that management anticipates a continued high demand for AI infrastructure. The next challenge, meanwhile, is whether Dell can maintain its profitability while fulfilling a record backlog and controlling growing component prices. Wednesday’s trade reflected that uncertainty. Despite its remarkable performance, Dell first sold off, but by the closing bell, it had recovered. The question of whether Dell can profit from the AI boom is no longer the most important for investors. The question now is whether the business can continue to develop profitably enough to meet Wall Street’s demands. Related: Anthropic’s $150 Wall Street target comes with a $900B catch

title: Jeff Bezos makes a $200 million move involving Amazon stock
summary: The SEC filing shows this was no ordinary transaction.
content: When a company founder transfers shares valued at nearly $200 million in a week, most investors start looking for signs of trouble. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings showed that Amazon Executive Chairman Jeff Bezos transferred 771,492 shares on Nov. 12 and 13, 2026. The batch was valued at approximately $198.9 million based on Amazon’s Nov. 16 closing price of $257.75, according to Nasdaq . This transfer, however, had nothing to do with Bezos exiting his position or signaling concern about the company he founded more than three decades ago. Also Read: How Jeff Bezos added $102 billion to his fortune in one month Bezos directed shares to nonprofits, not to the open market Bezos transferred 674,088 shares on Nov. 12 and another 97,404 on the following day, the SEC filing disclosed on Nov. 16. The Bezos Earth Fund received the second, smaller batch worth approximately $25.1 million, a Form 144 SEC filing confirmed . The foundation planned to sell those shares through Morgan Stanley after receiving them as a charitable gift from Bezos on Nov. 13. The remaining shares from the larger Nov. 12 transfer went to other nonprofit organizations not named in the public filings. Bezos originally acquired these shares on July 5, 1994, the date he incorporated the company that would eventually become Amazon. That was nearly three years before Amazon’s 1997 initial public offering , which means those shares have appreciated from a near-zero cost basis to current prices. Because these shares were donated, they never entered the open market, and no outside buyer was involved in the transfer. The transaction transferred ownership directly from Bezos to the charitable organizations, with Morgan Stanley handling the subsequent sale only on behalf of the Earth Fund. Amazon’s executive chairman has donated more than $629 million in shares this year Bezos has followed this pattern throughout 2026, donating more than 1,253,797 shares in May and another 415,580 shares in late August . Those earlier batches, combined with the November transfers, bring total 2026 charitable giving to at least 2.44 million donated shares valued at roughly $629 million. More Jeff Bezos: Jeff Bezos just made his boldest move yet, into soccer Jeff Bezos takes bold new turn amid $4B Amazon sell-off Jeff Bezos breaks his own Amazon record Bezos still directly holds more than 878 million Amazon shares worth about $226.4 billion despite this year’s charitable transfers, the Nov. 16 filing showed . This year’s charitable transfers represent less than 0.3% of that total stake, underscoring how small these donations are relative to his overall ownership. Two named recipients, Day 1 Academies and the Bezos Earth Fund, account for roughly 22.5% of this year’s donated shares, Fortune noted . The remaining gifts went to unnamed nonprofit organizations, leaving the full scope of Bezos’ charitable activity for 2026 partially unclear from the available filings. Bezos created the Earth Fund in 2020 with a $10 billion pledge to combat climate change by 2030. The fund had distributed about $2.4 billion through late September 2026, meaning it needs to average roughly $1.8 billion annually to reach the goal, Fortune reported. Jeff Bezos has donated at least $629 million in Amazon shares to charity in 2026 while retaining an estimated $226 billion stake. Chesnot / Getty Images How donating appreciated shares creates different tax outcomes The tax code treats stock sales and charitable donations as fundamentally different transactions, with distinct financial outcomes for the person transferring the shares. Selling stock that has gained significant value triggers federal capital gains taxes on the difference between the original purchase price and the eventual sale price. Donating those same shares directly to a qualified charity allows the donor to claim a deduction for their fair market value if the shares have been held for more than a year, according to IRS Publication 526 . For founders with decades of unrealized gains, the tax advantages of giving shares to a charity rather than selling them are significant, Vanguard’s research found. Garrett Harbron, head of Advised Wealth Management Strategies at Vanguard, said donors keep more wealth in play through this route than they would by liquidating holdings and writing a check from after-tax proceeds. Not only do donors receive a tax deduction for the full fair market value of the securities, but they also avoid capital gains tax on the appreciation. The charity can sell those donated shares and keep the full proceeds because, as a tax-exempt organization, it owes no capital gains tax under the law . The IRS caps the deduction for long-term appreciated stock donated to public charities at 30% of adjusted gross income (AGI) in any given tax year. How to read large insider filings without jumping to conclusions Large insider transactions do not always mean executives are selling their shares, so the details behind each SEC disclosure matter for understanding what actually happened. Under SEC requirements , company insiders must file Form 4 disclosures identifying their transactions, with specific codes explaining the nature of each transfer. A “G” code identifies a charitable gift , meaning shares were transferred without an open-market sale. By contrast, an “S” code identifies a sale, which represents a different type of transaction with potentially different implications. These disclosures are publicly accessible through the SEC’s EDGAR database , allowing anyone to examine the transaction details behind major insider headlines. In Bezos’s case, the distinction between a charitable transfer and an actual sale helps explain why the nearly $200 million headline does not necessarily indicate a retreat from Amazon. title: Palo Alto Networks hit with fraud claims after blowout quarter
summary: A former Palo Alto Networks insider says the timing of certain deals was no accident. The company calls his claims meritless and plans to fight.
content: Anyone who has worked in sales knows the last week of a quarter. Managers call more, targets loom, and a deal that slips into next month feels like a personal failure. That pressure sits at the center of a lawsuit against Palo Alto Networks, which sells firewalls and security software to businesses and governments. Former regional vice president Dan McGill says he was fired for objecting to sales booked before customers signed off, Bloomberg reported . Also read: Palo Alto CEO says last week’s outages had an unlikely culprit The timing stings. The suit surfaced one week after Palo Alto posted a record first quarter . The deals date to 2023 and 2024, but they raise a question behind every strong quarter: how the company counts its sales. What the former executive says happened McGill spent about a decade at Palo Alto, later running its state, local and education sales in the East, the complaint says. His former boss, vice president Darren Estridge, is a co-defendant. The complaint centers on two New York government deals handled by resellers, the middlemen between Palo Alto and its customers. McGill says they were pushed to order before customers committed. A $4 million FDNY order was allegedly drawn up by a reseller at Estridge’s direction, without the fire department knowing. It counted toward fiscal 2023, the filing says, weeks before the department placed its own order. A $5 million multi-year deal with New York State’s IT office was allegedly booked in full in late April 2024. The state’s order covered only the first year, and the reseller was allegedly offered extra incentives. McGill also claims Palo Alto kept him until he closed a $75 million deal, its biggest ever in state and local government. He was fired in April 2025, told his behavior was “not conducive to corporate policy,” a reason he calls pretext. A Palo Alto spokesperson called the allegations “completely meritless” and said the company will defend itself, according to Stocktwits . None of the claims has been tested in court. The sums look small, which is why the details deserve a closer look. A former Palo Alto Networks regional VP alleges two New York government deals were booked early, before customers fully committed. The company denies it. SOPA Images / Getty Images The dollars are small, but the controls are not Together, the two deals come to about $9 million. Palo Alto now takes in more than that every day, based on its latest quarterly revenue of $3.44 billion. The telling detail is a routine internal check. At quarter-end, staff on reported deals got an email asking them to flag irregularities. Flagged deals were meant to be reviewed before reaching the financial statements, the complaint says. McGill says he asked to flag both deals and was told not to. If true, a safeguard built to catch deals like these was bypassed by a manager, and that matters more than the $9 million. McGill is seeking lost pay and damages in a whistleblower retaliation case, not a shareholder fraud suit. But he is suing partly under Sarbanes-Oxley, the law that also makes top executives certify financial reports. He alleges the FDNY deal flowed into SEC filings. Investors pay a premium for growth based on those filings. Any doubt about them shows up quickly in the stock. How the stock took the news The lawsuit arrived at an awkward moment. Palo Alto’s revenue jumped 39% in the quarter ended Oct. 31, according to its earnings release . The standout was next-generation security ARR, annualized revenue from active contracts for newer products, which rose 66%. It tracks how much recurring business is under contract. Management also raised its full-year forecast. Before the news broke, the stock was up 93% this year. Bloomberg’s report landed just after Wednesday’s close. Early after-hours figures varied, but Stocktwits reported a drop of roughly 5%, erasing much of the post-earnings rally. Palo Alto is also buying AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5 billion , paid entirely in stock. Buying growth with shares works best when those shares are trusted. With markets closed for Thanksgiving, Friday’s shortened session gives the first regular-hours read. One evening of after-hours trading settles nothing. The bigger question is what the case could reveal. More Palo Alto: Palo Alto CEO wants AI labs out of the ‘fear-mongering business’ Palo Alto Networks CEO drops blunt take on AI slowdown calls Palo Alto CEO has urgent warning for anyone using AI Fast growth makes clean books matter more Software investors rarely see deals one by one. They lean on metrics Palo Alto defines itself, like next-generation security ARR. Those metrics only work if the market trusts how each deal gets counted. That is why a $9 million dispute over years-old deals can still move a stock this large. The fight is older than it looks. McGill filed with the Labor Department’s OSHA in September 2025 and sued after more than 210 days without a decision, the filing shows. If the suit survives early motions, discovery could pull internal messages into the case. Palo Alto’s next report, for the quarter ending Jan. 31, is the nearest checkpoint. Across software, the fastest growers earn premium valuations on numbers investors cannot fully verify. The test for Palo Alto is whether its quarter-end paperwork holds up as well as its quarter-end results. title: Astera Labs is suddenly back in the AI spotlight after rough patch
summary: The AI connectivity chipmaker's stock is making moves that have Wall Street watching.
content: Astera Labs (ALAB) went through a rough five-month period in 2026. The stock closed at $483.02 on June 30 and touched an intraday high of $499.48 that same day. However, by Nov. 20, it had fallen all the way to $180.35. That’s a drop of about 64% in just five months. The reasons for the large decline were valuation concerns and pressure from competitors. Broader pullbacks in the semiconductor sector also affected the stock. Then ALAB gained back some of that lost ground on Nov. 23, only to quickly give back most of those gains. Why Astera Labs lost nearly two-thirds of its value in 5 months The value of chip stocks dropped in October and early November. Then on Nov. 2, Marvell Technology announced that it would combine with Lumentum in an all-stock deal valued at $115 billion. That news left investors unsure about which company would win the booming market for AI server links. Also read: Anthropic IPO may pose a disturbing problem for retirement accounts Even though Astera announced strong earnings on Nov. 3, people still sold the stock. Over the next two trading days, ALAB fell 23%. And on Nov. 5 alone, the stock dropped 19.6% during a wider sell-off in the AI infrastructure sector, according to Trefis . On Nov. 12, Nvidia surprised investors by announcing that Jensen Huang had resigned as chief executive. The news pulled down many AI chip stocks, Astera included. Astera Labs makes the chips that let AI servers move data between processors, memory, and storage. Cheng Xin / Getty Images What Astera Labs actually makes, and why it matters Astera Labs makes the chips that AI servers use to communicate at very high speed. When an Nvidia GPU needs to move data to memory or to another chip inside a server rack, it often does so through Astera silicon. That’s why the company’s products are becoming more valuable, with that value showing up in its numbers. The Scorpio family of switch chips became Astera’s largest product line in the third quarter. On the company’s earnings call , it shared that the product line passed $1 billion in annualized revenue. Related: Target, Kohl’s Veterans Day deals expose budget strain The newer Orion rack design is also making waves, as it can connect up to 160 AI chips in a single pod. Astera’s management said on the earnings call that a fully loaded 80-GPU Orion rack holds more than $100,000 worth of Astera content. “Astera Labs delivered outstanding Q3 2026 results, with record quarterly revenue of $584.9 million, up 49% sequentially and up 154% year-over-year, with broad-based growth led by Scorpio,” CEO Jitendra Mohan said, according to finviz . His main point was that in 2027, more AI server racks should carry more Astera silicon inside them. That should lift the company’s revenue per rack. What sparked the Nov. 23 rebound On Nov. 23, ALAB jumped about 23% to close around $222.12 amid a broader rally in the semiconductor sector. The rebound was triggered by news that Jensen Huang had been reinstated as Nvidia’s chief executive, CNBC reported. More AI Stocks: A scandal like the one haunting Nvidia just reached AMD, its biggest rival BofA reveals how Walmart will win shoppers heading into Christmas CoreWeave stuns Wall Street as Nvidia scandal deepens “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners, and customers,” Chairman Harvey C. Jones said, according to Nvidia’s filing with the SEC . As a result, chip stocks related to AI infrastructure rallied. What investors should consider before chasing the bounce The Nov. 23 bounce does not remove the concerns that made ALAB shares drop. The increase was mostly driven by the Nvidia news. Astera still derives most of its revenue from a small number of major U.S. cloud companies, and the company’s research costs are rising. It also faces growing competition from Broadcom and Marvell. In addition, the stock is still not cheap, trading at about 20 times its annual sales. However, Astera still has its positive aspects. The company holds $1.38 billion in cash with no debt, and keeps its gross margins above 72%. I believe the next real test for the stock will come when the company reports its fourth-quarter 2026 results in February 2027. The mass production of its Leo 2 memory controllers, expected in mid-to-late 2027, might also play an important role in lifting the stock’s value. title: Follow the smart money: 2 tech stocks billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller just bought
summary: Druckenmiller's family office boosted two tech stakes. See what the 13F data shows and what investors can't see in it.
content: Every quarter, investors get a peek at what some of Wall Street’s best-known names own. When a famous investor increases exposure to a stock, people are bound to take notice. Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller’s latest snapshot has two such moves. In one tech company, his firm’s share count jumped more than fivefold. In another, it nearly tripled. One company helps people build video games, and the other is a data storage company. Both companies expect artificial intelligence to help drive revenue higher over the next few years. Who is Stanley Druckenmiller? Druckenmiller is a billionaire investor and former hedge fund manager. He founded Duquesne Capital Management in 1981 and ran it until 2010, according to his CNBC profile . Also Read: Stanley Druckenmiller dumps entire $120M Alphabet stake to buy gold mining stock He also spent more than a decade at George Soros’ firm, where he was lead portfolio manager of the well-known Quantum Fund. Today, Druckenmiller is chairman and chief investment officer of Duquesne Family Office, according to Bloomberg . Large money managers must list certain holdings every quarter on Form 13F. The report is due within 45 days after the quarter ends, according to the Securities and Exchange Commission . Unity stock is a sizable bet Unity Software led Duquesne’s percentage increases in the 13F data reviewed. The investment firm added 3.2 million shares in Q3, an increase of 436% year over year. The position is worth $161.9 million or 3.66% of the total portfolio. Unity (U) offers tools for building games and also runs an ad business that helps publishers find players. Its engine is Unity Vector, an AI system that predicts which games users are likely to engage with. More Wall Street: Arista Networks stock gets fresh backing from Jim Cramer and Wall Street Oracle stock sinks as Wall Street confronts a $20 billion AI problem Wall Street just got a candid look at who is winning the AI race Valued at a market cap of $21.4 billion, Unity stock is down 74% from all-time highs but continues to grow at a steady pace. In Q3, it reported : Strategic revenue, a headline company measure, of $597 million, an increase of 59% year over year Vector revenue growth of 126% YoY and 40% sequentially GAAP net income of $122 million Record free cash flow of $220 million CEO Matt Bromberg wants investors to see beyond ads and emphasized. “We are not an ad network. We are an authoring platform.” Bromberg calls its business model a flywheel, which starts with making games easier to create with AI. This, in turn, attracts more creators who launch more games and make more use of Unity’s tools. But more games bring a new headache, which is getting noticed. As the shelves get crowded, publishers have a greater need to reach the right players, which should drive demand for the ad business. AI may also shorten the path between those two steps. In the past, developers had to seek out Vector, download its software, and set it up. In the new world of building through AI prompts, Bromberg says Vector and other Unity services connect as soon as a game is created. Unity’s daily active users have risen 25% since early August, when it opened its platform to AI coding agents. For the fourth quarter, Unity expects strategic revenue to grow 65% to 67% from the prior year. It sees Vector rising 21% to 23% from the third quarter, and Bromberg cautioned that not every quarter will bring 40% growth. Given estimates compiled by TIKR , analysts forecast free cash flow to expand from $404 million in 2025 to $2.7 billion in 2030. If Unity stock is priced at 20x forward FCF, it could surge 157% within the next three years. Stanley Druckenmiller, CEO of Duquesne Family Office, raises its stake in Unity and Seagate. Bloomberg / Getty Images Seagate stock rides the data boom Seagate Technology (STX) is the larger of the two positions. Duquesne’s stake climbed from 122,000 shares to 341,790, up 180.16%. The holding is worth more than $300 million and accounts for 7% of the portfolio. Together, Seagate and Unity make up almost 11% of the total portfolio. Seagate makes hard drives, and big data centers drive top-line demand. Its case is simple: AI creates and reuses huge amounts of data, which needs to be stored. In fiscal Q1 (ended in September), revenue rose 61% year over year to $4.2 billion, while adjusted earnings almost tripled to $7.68 per share. Adjusted gross margin rose to 57.8% from 52.7% in the prior quarter. Related: Seagate’s booming business comes with an unexpected twist Customers are also planning far ahead. Most of Seagate’s supply of high-capacity data center storage is already allocated under long-term agreements through calendar 2028. CEO Dave Mosley sees more room to run. “We believe we’re still in the early days of a multiyear growth phase,” he said on the Oct. 27 call. For the December quarter, Seagate expects about $4.8 billion in revenue, give or take $100 million. The midpoint implies 70% yearly growth. It also expects adjusted earnings of $9.20 per share, plus or minus 20 cents. EPS is projected to more than double from $40 in fiscal 2027 to $84 in 2029. If the tech stock is priced at 10 times earnings, it could surge 80% within the next two years. What 13F filings don’t tell investors Before you follow the smart money, remember that a 13F looks in the rearview mirror. The data here don’t show what Duquesne paid, why it bought, or whether it still owns these shares. However, the two tech stocks continue to grow at a stellar rate and are expanding profit margins and cash flow. Treat Druckenmiller’s moves as a starting point for research, then weigh the risks yourself. title: Jim Cramer offers an unusual explanation for Nvidia stock’s price
summary: That expensive price tag hides a twist.
content: If you’ve read my most recent piece on veteran analyst Jim Cramer revamping his Nvidia ( NVDA ) stock price target to $199 after CEO Jensen Huang’s return , you probably already know how quickly the sentiment around AI’s poster child can flip. Just days ago, investors were cheering on Huang’s return and wondering whether the stock’s leadership overhang had cleared. Then came a fresh governance jolt on Wednesday, Nov. 25, sending shares sliding nearly 4% to $149.30, Bloomberg reported . Nvidia stock’s now sitting around 39% below its October peak, and plenty of everyday investors are wondering if it’s a classic high-growth trap. On the Nov. 25 episode of CNBC’s “Mad Money,” Cramer offered a counterintuitive answer. Sparked by a caller’s Warren Buffett question, he laid out a surprising explanation for why Nvidia’s price tag has consistently fooled Wall Street for more than a decade, and could potentially drive it next. Why Jim Cramer says Nvidia stock looks expensive until it looks cheap In a “Mad Money” segment shared by CNBC on Nov. 25 , a caller named Ned from Ohio quizzed Cramer about a classic Warren Buffett warning about high-growth companies carving out their own stability, asking whether Nvidia fits the mold. Cramer didn’t hesitate. “Well, okay, Nvidia is a really great example,” Cramer replied. “Let me tell you why. Because when you look at Nvidia on forward earnings, on the estimates, it always looks expensive. And then it so far trumps those estimates that when you look backward, it turns out that the stock was selling at a remarkably low price during its bubble. And that’s been the secret to Nvidia literally since 2012. Incredible. It just keeps doing that.” Recent numbers underscore Cramer’s point clearly. On Nov. 17 , Nvidia reported fiscal Q3 2027 sales of $115.8 billion, up 103% year over year and comfortably above LSEG’s $109.10 billion consensus, as Data Center sales shot up 110% to $107.6 billion and GAAP net income jumped 105% to $65.3 billion. Similarly, adjusted diluted earnings rose to $2.68 per share, above the $2.48 expected, while management guided Q4 revenue to $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, ahead of Wall Street’s $125.25 billion forecast, and bumped its fiscal 2028 growth outlook to 75%. Because earnings have expanded so rapidly, the chipmaker’s stock trades at under 16 times trailing Non-GAAP earnings, below the S&P 500’s 20.3 multiple, and 62% below its own five-year average, as reported by Seeking Alpha . Jim Cramer says Nvidia’s earnings growth can make expensive valuations look misleading. picture alliance / Getty Images What Warren Buffett’s Berkshire letters actually say about hypergrowth Layering Warren Buffett into an Nvidia debate adds much-needed context, and a subtle twist investors shouldn’t overlook. When Ned referenced companies that “eventually forge their own anchor,” he was referencing a famous passage from Warren Buffett’s 1989 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter. More Nvidia: Microsoft just gave Nvidia shareholders a reason to pay attention Nvidia has a stake in SpaceX that came from an unexpected place Nvidia’s $12.9 billion deal could shape the AI apps you use In it, Buffett warned against extrapolating blistering growth forever. “In a finite world, high growth rates must self-destruct. If the base from which the growth is taking place is tiny, this law may not operate for a time. But when the base balloons, the party ends: A high growth rate eventually forges its own anchor.” Yet Buffett also understood why an expensive stock price multiple could look dirt cheap in hindsight. In his 1992 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter , Buffett broke down the artificial wall between growth and value investing, writing: “In our opinion, the two approaches are joined at the hip: Growth is always a component in the calculation of value.” That tension effectively defines Nvidia stock right now. So far, the chipmaker has efficiently defied Buffett’s 1989 gravitational pull by pairing tremendous scale, backed up a 74.8% GAAP gross margin and arguably the fastest product ramp in company history for its Vera Rubin NVL72 platform. The contrarian risk to Cramer’s thesis and how investors should respond That said, the bullishness comes with a challenge. Nvidia’s consistently delivered smashing quarterly results, but it might struggle to beat expectations when investors demand nearly inch-perfect results. On Nov. 25, Nvidia shares dropped 3.91% after S&P Global Ratings placed its AA credit rating on CreditWatch Negative over governance concerns. Nvidia also expects Q4 gross margins to drop from 74.8% to 71% to 72% as Vera Rubin production expands. At the same time, China data center revenue remains uncertain, and Nvidia depends too much on major cloud customers developing their own chips. Cramer himself warned about such risks: “When everybody expects the same outcome in the stock market, there’s a very good chance it won’t play out as expected because it’s already priced in,” he warned. His $199 Nvidia price target points to a superb 33.3% upside from its Nov. 25 close. Still, investors need to remember his advice. “Discipline must always trump conviction. That means that we like to start trimming at 20% up. We’ll trim between 5% and 10% and another 20%.” That means watching margins and cloud spending is critical. title: Michael Burry just made a surprising call on the Nasdaq 100
summary: The man who called the housing crash just flipped his biggest market bet. His next target might surprise you.
content: Michael Burry was still doubling down against the Nasdaq 100 as recently as Nov. 12. When the index bounced off the 27,000 level that day, he added to his puts and summed up the rally in three words: “Behold the bull-trap,” according to TheStreet. Now that bet is gone, and the timing is hard to ignore. The Nasdaq 100 fell 20% from its October peak on an intraday basis on Nov. 25, officially hitting bear market territory. Burry used the slide to walk away from the trade and lean the other way. For the first time in a while, the investor famous for betting against the housing market holds more long positions than short ones. The shift is a notable turn for someone who spent much of 2026 positioning for a correction. His next move is already taking shape, and it points squarely at a stock that just had one of its biggest days in more than two decades. Why Michael Burry walked away from his Nasdaq puts The puts he just sold were not small. In his Nov. 12 Substack post, Burry doubled his Nasdaq 100 put position with contracts expiring in early 2027 at strikes roughly 20% below the index. He also said he expected a significant correction in chip and tech stocks before mid-2027. Also read: Michael Burry sees a serious problem Wall Street may be overlooking He went after chip stocks the same week. Burry bought back part of his VanEck Semiconductor ETF puts and named AMD and Broadcom as possible winners if Nvidia’s grip on the market loosens. “I stick with SMH,” he wrote, explaining why he picked that fund over a rival ETF whose top holdings are those two chipmakers, according to TheStreet. So why fold now? With volatility up and the market falling, Burry said puts tied to the AI buildout have become very expensive, which leaves outright short sales as his main bearish tool. He called shorting stocks “asymmetric the wrong way,” and said his only remaining bearish options are on Palantir and MetLife, according to Bloomberg. He’s also keeping plenty of dry powder. About 25% of his portfolio sits in cash. The rest is spread across stocks he considers undervalued, long-dated call options and preferred shares, which gives him room to buy if prices keep sliding. Nvidia’s comeback and the $200 line Nvidia gave him a reason to stay nimble. The board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Nov. 23, and the stock jumped 31.48% to $165.05, its best single-day gain in more than two decades, adding nearly $1 trillion in market value, according to The Motley Fool. Few investors saw that kind of reversal coming just 11 days after Huang stepped down. Burry caught a small piece of that rally. His Nvidia call options have doubled, but he has no plans to stay bullish on the chipmaker for long. “My plan is to short Nvidia again nearer $200/share during a period of market optimism,” he wrote. In other words, he wants the crowd to get excited first. That fits what he said earlier in November. In a Nov. 10 post, Burry wrote that he was “not tempted as a long-term hold from here,” and described his December call options as a hedge rather than a play for gains, according to TheStreet. He also argued that Nvidia’s competitive edge could shrink over the next five years. Nvidia’s troubles aren’t over, either. Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott asked Huang to testify at a public hearing on Dec. 3 and warned that subpoenas could follow if he refused. Lawmakers want answers about whether Nvidia’s advanced chip exports to China got enough scrutiny. Michael Burry was still doubling down against the Nasdaq 100 as recently as Nov. 12. Bloomberg / Getty Images Where Burry is putting his money His biggest bets are far from Silicon Valley. MercadoLibre and Temple & Webster each make up more than 10% of his portfolio, and he said he would buy more MercadoLibre if it dropped another 20%. One is a Latin American e-commerce giant, the other an Australian online furniture seller. JD.com rounds out his top three, and he holds call options on it that run as late as 2029. The Chinese retailer returned to revenue growth in the third quarter, with sales up 3.5% and an operating profit replacing a loss from a year earlier. The rest of the list is a mix of familiar names. Adobe, Birkenstock, Deckers, Lululemon and PayPal sit alongside Hong Kong-listed BYD, Tencent and Meituan, and together they make up slightly more than a fifth of the portfolio. Very few of them are the high-flying AI names that powered the market’s run. More Wall Street: Arista Networks stock gets fresh backing from Jim Cramer and Wall Street Oracle stock sinks as Wall Street confronts a $20 billion AI problem Wall Street just got a candid look at who is winning the AI race His shift toward value didn’t come out of nowhere. Back in May, Burry said the market felt like the last months of the 1999-2000 bubble, at a time when the Shiller CAPE ratio stood at 40.3, a level last seen near the dot-com peak, Fortune reported. What it means for everyday investors Nvidia’s rebound looks huge, but it hasn’t erased much of the damage. Even after the Nov. 23 surge, the stock still sat roughly 31% below its Oct. 6 record close. Burry’s $200 target shows how far it would need to climb before he bets against it again. His moves can also flip fast. Earlier this November, Burry cut his Caterpillar puts by 75% after they roughly quadrupled, and he repurchased chip-fund puts he had trimmed only days before. He shares his trades after making them, so anyone copying him is always a step behind. The bigger message is about patience. Burry isn’t calling a bottom in tech, and he still expects a significant correction in chip and tech stocks before mid-2027. For now, he would rather own cheap stocks and hold cash than pay up for expensive protection. Related: Jim Cramer sends strong words to stock market investors

title: Down 50%, is Micron stock a bargain buy or a value trap?
summary: Micron stock is down about 50%, despite record earnings and AI contracts in fiscal 2026.
content: Valued at a market cap of $680 billion, Micron reported record profits in fiscal 2026 (ended in August). However, the chip stock is down over 50% from its all-time highs. Investors are worried that the AI trade could unwind due to rising capital expenditures, higher debt levels, and elevated interest rates across the tech spectrum. Does this mean that the AI bubble is about to burst, driving Micron (MU) stock lower over the next 12 months, or is this cycle any different? Why is AI driving Micron demand? At Micron’s TomorrowX Summit talk on Nov. 18, moderator Gavin Baker recalled attending a Micron analyst day in Sun Valley, Idaho, in 2000. Also Read: David Tepper’s Micron bet raises a $32 billion question Memory was then a brutal business, and Micron Technology chief Scott DeBoer estimated the company had 10 to 15 competitors in DRAM, the fast working memory inside computers. Baker said the field is now really down to three. Powerful artificial intelligence (AI) processors often sit idle while they wait for data to arrive from memory. CEO Sanjay Mehrotra explained at the summit that computing power has advanced much faster than memory bandwidth over the past 20 years. Bandwidth measures how quickly data can move. To get more work from their processors, AI systems need more and faster memory. Mehrotra said demand remained robust and supply stayed tight. He also said 75% of 2027 was sold out. Micron earnings set new records In fiscal 2026, Micron reported revenue of $133.2 billion, an increase of 256% year over year, while adjusted earnings surged 811% to $75.52. It reported a gross margin of 81.1%, up from 22.4% in fiscal 2024. For the current first quarter of fiscal 2027, Micron guided to revenue of $61.5 billion, a forecast gross margin of 86.25%, and EPS of $38.15 per share. Notably, in fiscal Q4 of 2026, it reported a gross margin of 87%. Micron explained that higher employee incentive pay is a big reason for the expected margin dip. Moreover, management expects this quarter to be the low point for gross margin in fiscal 2027. Micron ended fiscal 2026 with $73.5 billion in cash and investments, against $5.2 billion of debt. It plans to increase shareholder returns starting Dec. 9, when certain CHIPS Act restrictions expire. Micron contracts could soften a downturn Micron had signed 26 strategic customer agreements as of Sept. 30. Several of these agreements are tied to five-year contracts. They are “take or pay” deals, which commit customers to set purchase volumes. Customers have also made $32 billion in financial commitments, mostly via cash deposits. Micron must return the deposits later if the minimum purchase terms are met. More Artificial Intelligence: AI investments fail when companies ignore the hard part of transformation Morgan Stanley issues a fresh warning about AI stocks CrowdStrike gives companies a ‘kill switch’ as bots go off script Demand for these deals appears intense. At the summit, Mehrotra offered this observation: “Customers wanted more commitment for supply than we were able to provide to them.” However, Micron estimates the agreements represent over 35% of revenue through 2030. About three-quarters of that slice has a set pricing framework, mostly with price floors and ceilings. The rest is priced periodically using market rates. Mehrotra said coverage could reach around 50%, or end up lower, which means a large share of future sales may sit outside these deals. Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra is bullish on strong demand Bloomberg / Getty Images Is Micron stock a value trap? On the earnings call, Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya said depressed memory valuations suggest people fear a 2027 peak, with new supply and customers trimming memory among the concerns. Baker noted that older supply deals often broke or burdened chip companies. However, Baker, who described himself as a small Micron shareholder, believes this time is different. Mehrotra pushed back on the peak fear. He expects industry supply to be much tighter in 2027 and 2028 than in 2026. Related: Intel CEO’s warning offers a 2027 signal for Micron investors Micron noted that memory per server is growing a bit more slowly than expected. But Mehrotra expects server shipments to rise by a high-teens percentage in both 2026 and 2027. New factories take time, too, and Micron doesn’t yet see when supply will catch up with demand. One key product is high-bandwidth memory (HBM), which stacks memory chips to enable faster data transfer. Micron called it one of the most complex chips ever built. Next comes stacking memory directly on processors, with management expecting multiple-layer versions to start arriving around 2028 or 2029. Micron stock: bargain or trap? Management makes a strong business case. However, if demand falls off a cliff, it will impact MU’s revenue, earnings, and cash flow. For instance, analysts forecast Micron ‘s sales to grow by 106.7% year over year to $275.3 billion in fiscal 2027 and by 15% to $316 billion in 2028. As demand normalizes, profit margins could narrow significantly over the next two years. Heavy spending also raises the company’s risk profile. Micron plans about $25 billion in capital spending in the first half of fiscal 2027, and the total could surge over $54 billion in the next 12 months. Before deciding to invest in MU stock, I’d watch these signals: Pricing: Micron expects price hikes to continue at a more moderate rate in fiscal 2027. Margins: Do they improve after the first quarter, as management expects? Contracts: Do coverage and customer commitments keep growing? Supply: Does the shortage outlook for 2028 hold as new factories advance? If those signals hold, MU stock is a top value stock to own in November 2026. Wall Street remains bullish on the mega-cap tech stock. Out of the 30 analysts covering MU stock , 28 recommend “Buy,” and two recommend “Hold”. The average Micron stock price target is $1,573, 150% above the current price. title: Novartis raises the stakes on 3 of its biggest drugs
summary: The drugmaker now expects eye-catching annual sales from its three fastest-growing drugs.
content: Novartis (NVS) told investors on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026, that Kesimpta, Scemblix, and Leqvio should bring in a combined $18 billion a year at their peak. The company previously forecasted a combined $14 billion. For the patients who rely on these medicines regularly, that increase signals that Novartis still expects progress in these drugs. The company might already have new clinical data in hand that could widen the conditions the medicines treat. The drugs have also seen an increase in demand. What Novartis told investors about its 3 top drugs CEO Vas Narasimhan , who has run Novartis since 2018, used the London event to update the company’s medium-term guidance. He now expects the company’s sales to grow by about 5% a year on average in constant currencies through 2031. That’s a reduction from the 5% to 6% range the company had set previously. Also read: Bank of America backs Pharvaris on breakthrough for rare swelling disease The main reason the company now expects a slower pace is that the second half of 2031, breast cancer drug Kisqali’s patent is set to expire. That means the drug will face U.S. generic competition from other companies. However, even with the slower pace, what really caught my attention was the $4 billion upgrade to the three flagship drugs. Novartis confirmed that Kesimpta’s peak sales target rose to $8 billion from $6 billion, while Scemblix and Leqvio were each lifted to $5 billion from $4 billion. The Swiss drugmaker lifted peak sales guidance on three top medicines at its Capital Markets Day in London. Marlon Trottmann / Getty Images The conditions Kesimpta, Scemblix, and Leqvio actually treat Each of Novartis’s flagship drugs treats serious chronic conditions. Kesimpta is a monthly self-injection for people with multiple sclerosis. Multiple sclerosis is a disease that slowly weakens the nerves and affects close to one million people in the United States, according to the National MS Society . Scemblix is a once-daily pill for chronic myeloid leukemia, which is a blood cancer that often needs years of ongoing treatment. The third drug is Leqvio, a cholesterol-lowering shot given just twice a year after the first few doses. Doctors turn to Leqvio for patients whose cholesterol count stays high, even after trying common statin pills. Related: Merck stock rises as its cancer strategy gets personal Demand for these three drugs has been climbing fast. According to Novartis , in the third quarter of 2026, Kesimpta sales rose 22% to $1.48 billion, Scemblix sales increased 67% to $593 million, and Leqvio sales rose 63% to $506 million. The patent pressure shaping this forecast The raised forecast arrives as Novartis handles what Narasimhan called “the largest loss-of-exclusivity impact in our history.” The company is facing a series of patent losses. A recent example is Entresto, a heart failure pill whose global sales fell about 50% in Q2 2026 after generic copies reached the market, according to an SEC filing. More Pharma Stocks: Unprecedented weight-loss drug craze pushing Lilly to near-record highs Amgen’s new drug could mean fewer shots for obesity patients Bank of America resets Eli Lilly stock target ahead of key event To cover that lost revenue, Novartis’s management pointed to more than 30 drug candidates in its pipeline. And 10 out of those drug candidates carry multibillion-dollar sales potential. The company also expects over 35 major trial readouts through 2031. That’s why Narasimhan said in his Q3 2026 earnings commentary that priority brands and launches “more than offset generic erosion, demonstrating the replacement power of the business.” How investors are reading the Novartis update Euronext reported that Novartis shares fell about 3.3% in Swiss trading on Nov. 19. But the stock remained up roughly 16% year to date. One reason for the drop was that some investors focused on the slower long-term growth range rather than the drug upgrades. Still, Novartis reaffirmed that its core operating margin, which was already at 41.6% in the third quarter, should return to 40% or higher by 2029. The company expects the margin to return as newer drugs grow and the pressure from generic products eases. The question on investors’ minds right now is whether Kesimpta, Scemblix, and Leqvio can keep growing fast enough to cover the Cosentyx and Kisqali drop in 2029 and 2031, respectively. title: Popular weight-loss drugs face lawsuits over alleged permanent vision damage
summary: Hundreds of patients allege the popular drugs caused a rare eye condition that can lead to permanent vision loss. The FDA is now requiring updated warning labels.
content: Whenever a new weight-loss drug gains popularity, I think much of the conversation tends to focus on how quickly it works, how much weight people can lose, and the side effects they might experience. I find it interesting how less obvious risks can get lost in that discussion, especially when they involve something important. Most people wouldn’t think to question whether a weight-loss injection could affect their vision. That trust is now central to a growing legal fight. According to Bloomberg , hundreds of patients allege that GLP-1 drugs such as Ozempic and Zepbound caused a rare eye condition that led to permanent vision damage, and that Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly did not adequately warn them. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration said on Nov. 9 that it will require safety labeling changes because of a “potential increased risk” of non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, or NAION. A label change is not a finding of cause. “The data do not establish a cause-and-effect relationship,” Novo said, according to Bloomberg, and Lilly said it will keep defending itself in court. These are allegations that have not been proven. Also Read: Eli Lilly’s Foundayo pill wins first European approval What GLP-1 patients allege, and what NAION is NAION is sometimes called an “eye stroke.” It can cause sudden, painless vision loss, usually in one eye. Cilette Mitchell, 64, told Bloomberg she started Ozempic in 2024 to lose weight and woke one morning with clouded vision in her right eye. She went to a hospital for tests and told doctors she was taking Ozempic. Because the drug carried no warning about sudden vision loss at the time, she says they did not take her off it. More Healthcare/Health: Mark Cuban says CVS breakup may not make prescriptions more affordable Medicare’s December 7 deadline shapes next year’s health costs Suze Orman warns 390,000 seniors on Medicare plan exit Within a few weeks, she says, she lost sight in her other eye and is now legally blind. She was diagnosed with NAION and is suing Novo. She says she can no longer work as a bank branch manager in San Diego and struggles with her balance. “If I had been informed, I would have never taken this medication, ever,” she said. Novo declined to comment specifically on her claim. What the FDA did, and what it did not The FDA said NAION has been reported with all GLP-1 drugs on the market, and will require updated labeling. Lilly said in a statement that the FDA’s communication did not reference findings specific to its medicines, and it has already updated prescribing information for its drugs, according to a federal database. The FDA’s process involves discussing the exact wording with manufacturers and could result in updated labels early next year. Related: Novo Nordisk CEO opens the door to major move for U.S. investors The science is unsettled. According to Bloomberg , studies examining a possible link have produced conflicting results. People with type 2 diabetes already face a higher risk of vision loss and NAION, which makes it hard for researchers to tell whether the drugs cause it or whether some patients are predisposed. Regulators in Europe and the U.K. already require some GLP-1s to carry a warning. Plaintiffs’ lawyers see the FDA’s move as significant. “The FDA has now recognized that the potential risk of NAION warrants a warning, and whether patients should have received that warning sooner is a central issue in these cases,” said Craig Silverman, who represents patients suing both companies. The courtroom picture More than 7,000 lawsuits have been filed in state and federal courts over the past three years, according to court records cited by Bloomberg . Most allege gastrointestinal injuries such as stomach paralysis, gallbladder disease, and pancreatitis. The cases are consolidated into two multi-district litigations, with roughly 4,300 federal cases before Judge Karen Spencer Marston in Philadelphia and about 2,200 in New Jersey state court. Related: Obesity titan could shake up Lilly and Novo after astonishing trial She is deciding which expert opinions are admissible on the gastro claims, and expects to address the NAION cases as soon as mid-2027. Last year she ruled for the companies by excluding two plaintiff experts and requiring a specific radiological test for gastroparesis claims, according to Bloomberg . Jury bellwether trials could come within two years. Neither side will discuss what a resolution might cost, though mass torts like this can end in settlements reaching billions, such as Johnson & Johnson ‘s proposed $5.5 billion talc settlement. Lilly’s Q3 revenue was $24.4 billion, up 39%, with Mounjaro up 65% in Q3 to $10.7 billion and Zepbound at $5.4 billion. Foundayo brought in $184 million. UCG / Getty Images What it means for Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly I covered the other side of this race when Novo CEO Mike Doustdar said Novo was “already in production mode” for CagriSema, and when Eli Lilly CEO Dave Ricks said Foundayo had one-third of new oral GLP-1 starts. Both stories assumed demand keeps rising. Use has nearly quadrupled since 2024, according to Gallup , with as many as 30 million Americans on one of these drugs. The business scale is large. Lilly ’s Q3 revenue was $24.4 billion, up 39%, with Mounjaro up 65% in Q3 to $10.7 billion and Zepbound at $5.4 billion. Foundayo brought in $184 million. Lilly raised full-year guidance to $91 billion to $92 billion. Novo ‘s Q3 sales rose 4% at constant exchange rates, with adjusted operating profit up 27%. For investors, the legal risk is slow and uncertain. For patients, the practical point is simpler. Sudden vision changes on any of these drugs should prompt a call to a doctor straight away. Ask about the new label and any eye-health risk factors, especially if you have diabetes. title: Elon Musk’s SpaceX stock giveaway hides a surprise for shareholders
summary: The $18 billion pledge comes with a catch.
content: Whenever a public company reveals an $18 billion stock giveaway, Wall Street’s first instinct is typically to flinch. SpaceX ( SPCX ) closed up 1.3% at $127.44 on Nov. 25, still 43.5% below its June 16 record intraday peak of $225.64 . And the last thing bruised retail and institutional shareholders want to see is a headline sounding like heavy dilution or an imminent insider dump. Yet SpaceX announced it would be contributing one newly issued Class A share to every currently active Trump Account , while CEO Elon Musk pledged to personally match the company’s gift once his lockup expires in June 2027. Based on around 72 million U.S. children, Reuters estimated the combined potential value at nearly $18 billion. Looking past the viral consumer headlines, however, the actual shareholder math delivers a genuine surprise. Why an $18 billion giveaway does not mean $18 billion in dilution I think the crux of the matter for SpaceX investors is pretty straightforward. A potential $18.35 billion stock gift doesn’t exactly equal $18 billion in shareholder dilution. Only 50% of the proposed giveaway involves newly created equity. Remember that 72 million is an estimate of the total number of U.S. children, not a confirmed count of active, funded accounts, so the headline figure is an illustrative potential value. Still, assuming 72 million recipients receive two shares each at the Nov. 25 $127.44 close, SpaceX would issue 72 million new Class A shares worth around $9.18 billion, while Musk would transfer 72 million existing shares worth another $9.18 billion. Against SpaceX’s 13.58 billion shares outstanding (13,581,063,709 in its Oct. 15 SEC filing , which implies a $1.73 trillion market capitalization), issuing 72 million new shares trims existing owners’ proportional stakes by just 0.53%, reducing a 1% position to roughly 0.9947%. Using nearly 70 million Trump Accounts opened through October, the combined value comes to around $17.84 billion, and dilution edges down to 0.51%. Musk’s matching transfer adds zero issuance dilution as those shares already exist. Even so, that 0.53% dilution isn’t cost-free. Unlike a typical stock offering, SpaceX collects zero cash for $9.18 billion in newly created stock, shifting a small sliver of economic and voting ownership to recipients. SpaceX plans new shares as Elon Musk pledges matching stock to children. Adam Gray / Getty Images The lockup reality check SpaceX shareholders cannot ignore Another important thing to understand is what the announcement does amount to. It neither pulls 144 million shares out of SpaceX’s 4.35 billion public float nor eliminates Musk’s June 2027 selling overhang. SpaceX’s newly issued stock never traded in today’s public float, and Musk’s personal contribution comes from locked insider holdings instead of open-market share purchases. Under SpaceX’s IPO prospectus , Musk’s special 366-day lockup expires June 12, 2027, covering around 6.4 billion beneficially owned shares. More Elon Musk: Elon Musk reportedly invests $1 billion in media giant Elon Musk makes an odd new promise about the Tesla Roadster Elon Musk doubles down on the Roadster with SpaceX thrusters Even if his transferred shares enter restricted accounts that defer a small slice of future selling beyond June 2027, 72 million shares represent around 1.1% of his position, leaving roughly 98.9% untouched. A far larger supply test is expected to hit next month. SpaceX’s IPO prospectus flags up around 797.6 million shares held by employees and early pre-IPO investors, perhaps over 11 times the giveaway’s newly issued stock, becoming eligible for release from 180-day lockup restrictions on Dec. 8, 2026. It’s imperative to understand that eligibility doesn’t guarantee that everyone will sell, as Mizuho analysts recently noted. What Treasury rules and unresolved fine print mean next Whether gifted SpaceX shares stay off the market for years depends a ton on Treasury rules. Under September 2026 regulations, qualifying Trump Account shares usually cannot be sold until five years after deposit or Dec. 31 of the year the child turns 17, whichever comes first. That means a five-year-old receiving shares in December 2026 might face restrictions through December 2031, while a 16-year-old’s restriction ends in December 2027. Some exceptions apply. But three questions remain. Musk’s personal gifts: Reuters said that SpaceX has yet to confirm whether Musk’s personal gifts in June 2027 will enter Trump Accounts or face the same restrictions. Treasury restrictions: Qualifying stock must be publicly traded and free of any existing resale restrictions, which complicates transfers of pre-IPO shares. Pending approvals: SpaceX says the giveaway still depends on account counts, record dates, and regulatory approvals. Musk wrote on X that “giving shares, which are stakes in the future economy, directly to the people is the way.” For SpaceX stock investors, the bigger questions are how the market handles the Dec. 8 lockup expirations and how Musk’s transfer actually works. title: How much GOOGL stock does Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai own?
summary: Sundar Pichai has worked at Alphabet for more than two decades and has served as CEO since 2019. Here’s how many Alphabet shares he owns.
content: Sundar Pichai is only the second CEO of Alphabet (formerly Google) since the company, which made internet search synonymous with its eponymous founding name, was created in 1998. Pichai was hired six years after Google got its start, and he has led product and engineering for Google’s products and platforms, including Search, Chrome, Maps, Android, Gmail, and Google Workspace. Since 2019, he has held CEO titles for the Google division and its holding company, Alphabet. Here’s how many Alphabet shares Pichai owns and how he accumulated them. How much of Alphabet does Sundar Pichai own? Pichai owns 3.2 million shares of Alphabet, according to an SEC filing in October 2026 . That amount consisted of direct ownership of 1,678,737 shares of Class C Capital Stock, 191,759 Class C Google stock units, and 227,560 shares of Class A common stock. Pichai’s indirect ownership included 1.1 million shares of Class C Capital Stock held in annuity trusts by him and his wife, Anjali. Class C shares, which use the ticker symbol GOOG, hold no voting shares, while Class A shares, which trade under the GOOGL symbol, have voting shares. Class B shares aren’t publicly traded but hold significant voting power, and almost all of that stock is held by founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin. Together, the two hold the majority of voting power over Alphabet. Related: How much ANT stock does Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei actually own? Is Sundar Pichai the largest individual shareholder of Alphabet? Sergey Brin and Larry Page are the largest individual shareholders of Alphabet, and their ownership is spread across the company’s three classes of stock. Brin holds 717.8 million shares in Class A, B, and C common stock through both direct and indirect ownership, based on an SEC filing in August 2026 , and that equates to almost 5.9% of the total 12.24 billion outstanding shares. Alphabet’s largest institutional shareholders Institutions own about 89.8% of Alphabet’s GOOGL stock, according to Nasdaq data . The Vanguard Group is the biggest holder, with 528.9 million shares, followed by BlackRock (459.0 million shares), and Vanguard Capital Management (384.8 million shares). Related: How much CRM stock does Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff actually own? How & when did Sundar Pichai accumulate his Alphabet stock? Pichai’s accumulation of Alphabet stock comes from his more than two decades of employment at Alphabet. Pichai, 53 years old, first joined Alphabet in 2004, when he served as head of product management and development, and rose through the ranks to become CEO of Google, the company’s services and cloud division. Then, in 2015, he became the CEO of Alphabet, Google’s holding company, succeeding Brin in 2019. How much stock does Sundar Pichai get as part of his compensation package? Not unlike many CEOs, Pichai takes a salary and gets incentives for meeting his company’s internal performance targets. In 2025, he received no bonuses or stock awards, but had a base salary of $2 million and $8.98 million in compensation, which included contributions to a 401(k) plan and personal use of company aircraft and a company car, according to Alphabet’s 2026 proxy statement . title: JPMorgan Chase launches 2-week mortgage rate sale
summary: You can receive a mortgage rate discount as high as 0.25% from Nov. 30 to Dec. 13.
content: High mortgage rates have been a major deterrent to buying a home in 2026. The 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 7.21% as of Nov. 25, according to Freddie Mac . Frankly, many Americans simply cannot afford monthly mortgage payments at that rate. But Chase Home Lending is offering prospective buyers and existing homeowners a limited-time opportunity to lower their mortgage rates. The mortgage and home-financing division of JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., is launching a two-week mortgage rate sale, from Monday, Nov. 30, through Sunday, Dec. 13. You could receive a rate discount as high as 0.25% on either a mortgage for a new home or a refinanced mortgage. “As millions of holiday shoppers look for the best online deals, the biggest purchase most people will ever make deserves the same kind of careful shopping,” Erik Schmitt, head of consumer direct sales at Chase Home Lending, said in a statement shared with TheStreet. How the Chase mortgage rate sale works If you get a mortgage or refinance with Chase, you could qualify for a rate discount of up to 0.25%. The actual discount varies depending on the borrower’s location and loan type, so not everyone will qualify for the full 0.25% reduction. When I asked a Chase representative how these factors affect the discount, they recommended that customers speak with a Chase Home Lending Advisor about their specific situation. Read more: JPMorganChase drops $750B to fix U.S. housing crisis The representative confirmed that the promotion applies to both purchase and refinance mortgages, including conforming, jumbo, FHA, and VA loans. The rate discount just isn’t available on Chase home equity lines of credit (HELOCs). To qualify for the mortgage rate discount, you must lock in your rate with Chase during the promotional period from Nov. 30 to Dec. 13. However, you don’t have to close on a house during this period. You can lock in your mortgage rate on the Chase MyHome dashboard , at your local bank branch, or on the phone with a Chase Home Lending Advisor. Chase Bank is offering a 2-week mortgage rate sale on new and refinanced mortgages. James Leynse / Getty Images Combine the rate sale with other Chase mortgage discounts A 0.25% mortgage rate discount can go a long way toward making homeownership more affordable. The discount works even harder when you combine it with other Chase discounts and programs. And yes, Chase has confirmed that you can use the limited-time rate sale in addition to other Chase mortgage deals. Let’s say you take out a $400,000 mortgage at the current average 30-year mortgage rate of 7.21%. If you qualify for the full 0.25% Chase rate discount, your new mortgage rate would be 6.96%. That would drop your monthly principal and interest payment from $2,743 to $2,675. That saves you $68 per month, or $816 annually. Now, maybe you combine that with the Chase Home Lending Relationship Pricing Program . Relationship pricing mortgage rate discounts come in several tiers, but for this example, let’s say you qualify for the full 1% Relationship Pricing Discount . Combine that 1% discount with the limited-time 0.25% mortgage rate sale, and your new mortgage rate would be 5.96%. Now your new monthly payment drops to $2,410, saving you $333 monthly, or $3,996 yearly. (Keep in mind that these numbers represent monthly payments toward the mortgage principal and interest and exclude property taxes, homeowners insurance, and other housing costs.) More Housing Market and Mortgage Rates: Zillow predicts surprising mortgage rate, home price shifts Jeff Bezos says 2 policies drive up housing costs, and it’s ‘not hard to figure out’ Is the U.S. experiencing a housing recession? Experts weigh in Now for a different example. You might qualify for the Chase Homebuyer Grant , which provides up to $5,000 to eligible customers in certain parts of the U.S. You can put the $5,000 toward mortgage discount points, closing costs, and/or buying down your interest rate. By combining the 0.25% sale with the Homebuyer Grant, you could lock in an even better mortgage rate or combine a discounted rate with lower closing costs. With mortgage rates remaining above 7% , Chase’s limited-time promotion could give prospective homebuyers and homeowners looking to refinance an opportunity to secure a lower rate. And for borrowers who qualify for additional Chase mortgage discounts, the savings could be even greater. Just remember that you’ll need to lock in your rate between Nov. 30 and Dec. 13 to take advantage of the promotion. Related: Zillow reports stark housing market, homeownership shift

title: McDonald's new deals take aim at Chili's and convenience stores
summary: McDonald's is facing a value problem from both ends of the restaurant business, and it's trying a new approach.
content: McDonald’s faces pricing pressure in two different directions and has responded by adding two new value offers. On the one hand, the chain has to fend off convenience-store rivals, which offer lower prices and have the advantage of customers having to stop there to fill up on gas. In addition, McDonald’s has to compete with sit-down chains like Chili’s, which offers its “3 For Me” deal with a sandwich, fries, and an appetizer for $10.99. That makes it hard for McDonald’s, which was once seen as a value offering, to thread the needle. Now, the fast-food giant has added a $2 breakfast sandwich deal, along with a deal that offers customers a free medium order of fries. McDonald’s adds app-only deals McDonald’s has been working to restore its reputation as being a value leader. CEO Chris Kempczinski noted that in the U.S., performance improved as the quarter progressed, with comparable sales turning positive in September, following a slightly negative result in July and August, during the chain’s third-quarter earnings call . He attributed that to a change in the company’s value strategy. “That improvement followed a series of interventions we initiated during the quarter, restoring some digital offers to drive frequency with our most engaged customers, shifting marketing support toward proven value platforms, and stepping up our focus on restaurant-level execution,” he said. Now, the chain has launched two app-only deals. Free medium fries with $1 minimum purchase: Make any day fry day. Download the app and get ’em with your purchase of $1+. $2 Breakfast Sandwich : Now you want to wake up early. Download the app and choose from a Sausage, Egg & Cheese McGriddle, Bacon, Egg & Cheese Biscuit, Egg McMuffin, and more once a week only in the app — excludes delivery. Source: McDonald’s Both offers are valid one time a week through the end of the year at participating McDonald’s. The prices exclude tax and are not eligible for delivery. To get these deals, consumers must opt in to the chain’s rewards program. McDonald’s fights to take back its value crown Fast-food chains have been struggling to prove that they offer good value for a few years. More Americans have seen McDonald’s and other chains as a luxury, according to a 2024 LendingTree survey . Some of the key findings of that survey of 2,000 Americans include: Americans love fast food, but costs are forcing them to curb their cravings. Three in four Americans typically eat fast food at least once a week, but the majority (62%) say they’re eating it less due to rising prices. In fact, 65% of Americans have been shocked by the high price of a fast-food bill in the past six months. Are burgers the new Birkins? More than three-quarters (78%) of consumers view fast food as a luxury because it’s become increasingly expensive. Additionally, half of Americans say they view fast food as a luxury because they’re struggling financially. “McDonald’s… is supposed to be an inexpensive treat or a cheap fast-food fix. It is now a relatively expensive purchase, especially for a family,” GlobalData Managing Director Neil Saunders told USA Today . “Many don’t think it’s worth the money, so they cut back on dining there.” More Restaurants: 40-year-old fast-food franchisee files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy Landry’s rescues 9 restaurants from bankruptcy as closures mount Outback Steakhouse restaurant franchisee files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy RTM Nexus CEO Dominick Miserandino agrees that McDonald’s has lost its perception of being a cheap dining option. “McDonald’s used to be where you took the kids when you didn’t feel like cooking. When the bill starts to feel like you’ve taken the family out to dinner, you start thinking, well, where do we actually want to go? That’s a lousy question for McDonald’s to have people asking,” he told TheStreet. McDonald’s is offering $2 breakfast sandwiches. Shutterstock McDonald’s knows it has a value problem Kempczinski admitted during the Q3 call that McDonald’s has work to do on its value offering. He shared that the chain was testing “mix-and-match bundles that give customers greater choice and provide familiar ordering behaviors for prior buy one, add one offers.” That testing is ongoing at thousands of U.S. restaurants. “Our goal is to launch a new program nationally in early 2027,” he said. The CEO is encouraged by the early results. “We’ve already made significant improvements to address holistic value across our menu, which contributed to improvement in value and experience scores across our top 10 markets,” he added. Kempczinski also defended McDonald’s pricing compared to its rivals. “Today, our base menu pricing across the industry’s most popular menu items in chicken, beef, and beverages is generally below that of our nearest competitors. Our $5 and $6 meal deals remain industry standouts, and our Extra Value Meals on everyday fan favorites have become a proven platform to drive incremental sales,” he added. McDonald’s offers strong value if you pick and choose from its menu. I find it a little hard to justify the $10.89 my local McDonald’s is charging for a 10-piece Chicken McNuggets Meal or the $12.79 price of its Double Quarter Pounder Meal, but that same location has a buy-one-get offer for a 10-piece Chicken McNuggets, which costs $6.29. In theory, I could build two McNuggets meals for less than buying the combo off the menu. That’s confusing and not the best look for the chain, but it’s also a true value that consumers may embrace.
