title: Avoid these Black Friday tricks and scams
summary: Learn when to buy what, things you probably shouldn't buy, and how to avoid getting scammed.
content: Despite changing shopping patterns, Black Friday remains a massive day for retailers, though it has become just one part of an expanded season of retail deals. “Adobe expects U.S. online sales to hit $275.1 billion this holiday season (Nov. 1 to Dec. 31, 2026), growing 6.7% year-over-year (YoY). Cyber Week (the five-day period between Thanksgiving and Cyber Monday) is set to drive $47.5 billion online (up 7.4% YoY), representing 17.3% of the full holiday season spend,” according to Adobe’s 2026 forecast . A lot of those sales, however, will be online. “Cyber Monday (Nov. 30) is expected to set a new milestone for U.S. e-commerce, with consumers spending over $15 billion online in a single day ($15.1 billion, up 6.2% YoY). The second biggest day of the season will be Black Friday ($12.9 billion, up 9.2% YoY), which is growing faster than Cyber Monday — driven in part by having the biggest discounts for categories such as TVs, apparel, and appliances,” according to Adobe’s analysis. It’s a long holiday season, and there are better days than others to buy certain items. Shutterstock When to buy what during Thanksgiving shopping season Black Friday is Nov. 27 and Cyber Monday is Nov. 30. Adobe’s data showed that there are better days than others to buy certain items. Black Friday: Best for TVs, toys, apparel, appliances, and furniture. Cyber Monday : Best for electronics and computers. Thanksgiving Day: Best for sporting goods. Peak discounts : About 30% on electronics, 29% on toys, and 23% on TVs, computers, and apparel. Some shoppers are also buying things they need rather than just things they want. “While consumers have historically embraced holiday deals to buy gifts or adopt the latest gadgets, many are taking advantage of discounts to stock up on essentials. During Cyber Week, online sales of personal hygiene products are expected to jump 150% (compared to average sales levels in September 2026) and clothing basics by 210%. Other essentials set to see a boost include baby products (up 113%), pet products (up 93%), and household cleaning items (up 49%),” Adobe reported. Also Read: Struggling home goods chain closing more stores Shopping at major retailers is a way to avoid being scammed. Shutterstock Are there any products to avoid during the Black Friday season? As a former retailer who ran a large independent toy store, I’d suggest either buying traditional stocking stuffers well before the season, or filling stockings with practical items. Something like Play-Doh or a mini Magic 8-Ball generally costs more at my former store during the holiday season. The same might also be true for staples like decks of cards, Hot Wheels, and small games. There are also some categories to avoid this time of year, according to NBC Select : Winter clothes and shoes : Wait until end-of-season clearance sales in January and February Mattresses, furniture, and major home and kitchen appliances : Wait until three-day holiday weekend sales like Presidents’ Day Bed and bath linens, like sheets and towels : Wait until “white sales” in January and three-day holiday weekend sales like Presidents’ Day Fitness equipment : Wait until New Year’s sales in January. Holiday decor : Wait until after the holiday season to refresh your collection and save it for next year. ALSO READ: Walmart has a new plan to solve one of its customers’ biggest problems Holiday gift scams to watch for Back when I ran the toy store, a few days after Christmas, we would have customers bringing in train sets for us to repair. They were a brand we sold, but a lower-quality version sold in mall kiosks, or sometimes even in pop-up tents in parking lots. The manufacturer essentially put its name on a low-quality product that its actual dealers could not repair. That left a lot of people angry at us, but when our entry-level train set started around $299, and you bought one for $100, you probably should have known there was a catch. RILA Communities Foundation shared with TheStreet some other common scams to watch out for: Gift Card Scams: Scammers love gift cards because once you share the card number and PIN, your money can be gone in seconds. Never let anyone pressure you into buying a gift card or sharing the information on the back of the card. Counterfeits: Counterfeiters know holiday shoppers are looking for a great deal, and they use steep discounts, convincing photos, and look-alike websites to lure consumers into buying fake and sometimes dangerous products. Before you buy, take a closer look at who is actually selling the item, check the seller’s history and reviews, and be suspicious of prices that are dramatically lower than you would expect. Watch for misspelled brand names, poor-quality images, unusual packaging, vague product descriptions, and websites or sellers you don’t recognize. Stolen products: Beware of online sellers with little or no verifiable history and prices that are substantially lower than those offered by established retailers can indicate stolen products being resold. This is a known tactic for organized retail crime rings. A low price may be legitimate, but consumers should independently verify the seller before making a purchase. Be especially cautious when a seller pressures you to pay through a wire transfer, cryptocurrency, gift card, or other payment method that may offer limited protection. Scammers also set up fake gift-card balance-checking websites to capture card numbers and PINs. Check a balance through the website or phone number printed on the card, not through a link in a search result, ad, text, or email. “More than one-third of consumers say they have experienced at least one holiday scam tactic in recent years,” according to data shared with TheStreet by Bank of America. Scammers are also using artificial intelligence to make fake retailer and delivery-service websites look convincing. Check the seller’s history and contact details, avoid links in unsolicited messages, and contact your bank immediately if you believe your financial information has been compromised. title: Another movie theater chain files Chapter 11 bankruptcy
summary: Scene One Entertainment also operates a 75-year-old amusement park.
content: Movie theater chains have struggled in their battle against streaming services such as Netflix, which launched in 2007, as domestic box office revenue plummeted from a peak of $11.4 billion in 2019 to about $8.8 billion in 2025, according to data from commercial real estate feasibility consultant MMCG Invest . Another major factor that led to the downturn in movie theater revenue was the Covid-19 pandemic, which shut down indoor theaters in 2020. Theaters have not recovered from that downfall. Movie theater chains continue to face declining revenue that has forced certain companies to file for bankruptcy protection. Antonio_Diaz / Getty Images Scene One Entertainment files Chapter 11 And now, movie theater chain and iconic amusement park owner Scene One Entertainment Parks LLC has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, as the owner had difficulty securing financing for its businesses. The Schenectady, N.Y.-based owner of a chain of eight movie theaters in New York, Colorado, Connecticut, and New Hampshire, and Huck Finn’s Playland in Albany, N.Y., filed its petition, along with nine affiliates, in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of New York on Nov. 22, seeking to restructure their debts. “As part of our ‘North Star ‘ to provide the best moviegoing experience in each market we serve, we have taken a critical step by filing for bankruptcy protection to secure our company’s future and ensure a path to true profitability,” Scene One Entertainment said in a statement, according to WETM-TV . Scene One Entertainment listed up to $50,000 in assets and $1 million to $10 million in debts in its Subchapter V petition. Company faced financing difficulties “A reality of our business, much like many others, is that access to capital is limited due to market conditions,” Scene One said in the statement. “Unfortunately, this has been determined to be the best path forward to restructure our debts and for our company to continue to grow, thrive, and provide the very best of Hollywood features, independent films, and family entertainment for years to come. Bottom line: we’re not going anywhere,” the statement said. Scene One Entertainment said it has no plans to close any of its businesses. All locations remain open “It is our intention that each of our locations will remain open during this financial restructuring, especially with a dynamic slate of features coming out this season starting this week,” the statement said. Scene One Entertainment was founded in 2023 by its owner and CEO Joseph Masher, who added Huck Finn’s Playland amusement park to his portfolio of movie theaters that same year, according to the company’s website. Debtor owns 8 movie theaters Scene One Entertainment operates eight movie theaters, including Market Arcade 8 in Buffalo, N.Y.; Spectrum 8 in Albany, N.Y.; Wilton Mall Cinemas in Saratoga Springs, N.Y.; Movieland 6 in Schenectady, N.Y., Greenville Drive-In in Greenville, N.Y., New Canaan Playhouse in New Canaan, Conn., Gilford Cinema 8 in Gilford, N.H., and Isis Colorado in Aspen, Colo. Masher planned to add 100 movie screens to his company’s portfolio in 2026, according to the company website, but financial issues led to the bankruptcy filing instead. Huck Finn’s Playland opened in 1951 in Latham, N.Y., and its original owners operated the amusement park until selling to furniture store Huck Finn’s Warehouse in 2014. The home furnishings retailer operated the amusement park until Scene One Entertainment bought Huck Finn’s Playland nine years later. title: Sheetz cuts gas prices as Shell, 7-Eleven offer savings for holidays
summary: Major gas station chains are rolling out limited-time holiday deals and loyalty rewards.
content: Gasoline prices are finally falling, just as millions of Americans prepare to hit the road for Thanksgiving. The national average for regular gasoline dropped to approximately $3.61 per gallon on Nov. 19, according to AAA, down about 68 cents from a month earlier. However, drivers are still paying roughly 54 cents more per gallon than they were at the same time last year. It becomes especially important as we are into Thanksgiving week, when AAA expects 72.9 million Americans to travel by car between Nov. 24 and Nov. 30. With millions of drivers looking to reduce the cost of their holiday trips, major gas-station chains are offering new promotions alongside their existing loyalty rewards. Sheetz is among the latest to announce a Thanksgiving-specific discount, while Shell, Chevron, 7-Eleven, and other retailers are offering savings ranging from a few cents to $1 per gallon. But there is a catch: Some of the largest discounts require accumulated loyalty points, multiple visits or enrollment in a paid membership. Sheetz announces new Thanksgiving gas discount Convenience-store chain Sheetz announced on Nov. 24 that it will offer customers 20 cents off per gallon on fuel purchases from Wednesday, Nov. 25, through Monday, Nov. 30. The Thanksgiving promotion, confirmed to NACS , applies to all fuel grades except high-flow diesel at more than 850 locations, though Maryland stores are excluded due to state regulations. The discount is limited to 25 gallons per transaction, but customers can use the promotion multiple times during the six-day period. More Retail: Struggling home goods chain closing more stores Verizon makes changes to be more like T-Mobile used to be Home Depot drops generous offers as customers grow harder to win To redeem the offer, customers must add it under the OFFERZ tab in the Sheetz app, scan their My Sheetz Rewardz membership at the pump and accept the discount when prompted. The company also allows customers to combine the holiday promotion with other eligible My Sheetz Rewardz offers for additional savings. For a driver purchasing 15 gallons of gasoline, the 20-cent discount translates to $3 in savings. A 25-gallon purchase would save $5 before any additional rewards are applied. Sheetz is also offering My Sheetz Rewardz members one free self-serve hot or iced coffee of any size through Nov. 29, with one redemption per member. Sheetz is not the only convenience-store chain introducing a holiday-specific fuel promotion. Tennessee-based Weigel’s is offering MyWeigel’s Rewards members 25 cents off per gallon on Thanksgiving Day, Nov. 26. The limited-time promotions come as other major fuel retailers compete for drivers with introductory discounts and ongoing rewards. Which gas stations are offering discounts ahead of Thanksgiving? Some retailers are offering short-term holiday promotions, while others provide incentives for new loyalty members or ongoing discounts for returning customers. Here’s how the major programs compare. Company Advertised fuel savings Key conditions Sheetz 20¢ per gallon, Nov. 25–30 My Sheetz Rewardz; up to 25 gallons per transaction; excludes Maryland Weigel’s 25¢ per gallon on Nov. 26 Thanksgiving Day only; MyWeigel’s Rewards membership Kroger Up to $1 per gallon Must accumulate 1,000 rewards points Circle K Up to $1 per gallon Requires accumulating qualifying visits Shell 10¢, 20¢ and 30¢ per gallon First three qualifying fill-ups for new members Chevron and Texaco 25¢ per gallon on up to five fill-ups New rewards members; offer expires after 90 days 7-Eleven 25¢ per gallon on three fill-ups Promotional text offer; separate welcome rewards available Walmart+ 10¢ per gallon Active paid membership at participating stations Amazon Prime / BP 10¢ per gallon Linked Prime and earnify accounts Love’s 10¢ per gallon on gasoline Rewards app; location exclusions BP / Amoco 5¢ per gallon Free earnify membership Exxon / Mobil Points equivalent to 3¢ or 6¢ per gallon Earn points toward future rewards These programs have different redemption rules, and the advertised maximum discounts may not be available at every participating location. In particular, Sheetz and Weigel’s are offering time-limited Thanksgiving promotions, while most of the other discounts are part of programs available beyond the holiday. Kroger and Circle K offer some of the largest potential savings Kroger’s rewards program lets customers earn points from eligible grocery purchases, gift cards and other qualifying transactions. Every 100 points can be redeemed for 10 cents off per gallon. Drivers with 1,000 points can receive a $1-per-gallon discount on purchases of up to 35 gallons. For a driver buying 15 gallons, that would mean $15 in savings. However, reaching that maximum requires building up points before filling up. Kroger also offers a three-cent-per-gallon discount for rewards members at participating locations, even without redeeming points. Circle K’s Inner Circle program also advertises potential savings of up to $1 per gallon, but its program works differently. Members accumulate qualifying visits, including gasoline purchases of at least five gallons or eligible in-store purchases of at least $3. Those visits can be redeemed for various rewards, including fuel discounts. The available reward depends on the number of qualifying visits a customer has earned. Unlike Sheetz’s immediate holiday promotion, these maximum savings generally require customers to have already accumulated enough rewards. Thanksgiving brings limited discounts at select gas stations and convenience stores. Hispanolistic / Getty Images Shell, Chevron and 7-Eleven reward new customers Other companies are targeting drivers with discounts that can be accessed much sooner after enrollment. Chevron and Texaco are offering new rewards members 25 cents off per gallon on up to five qualifying fill-ups. The introductory offer expires 90 days after enrollment. Shell is offering new members 10 cents off per gallon on their first fill-up, 20 cents on their second and 30 cents on their third. The introductory rewards must be redeemed within 60 days of signing up and are limited to 20 gallons per fill-up. Shell also offers additional benefits through participating loyalty partners. For example, eligible AAA members linking their accounts can receive 30 cents off per gallon on their first fill-up and five cents off afterward, while eligible new AARP-linked members may receive 50 cents off on their first fill-up. Those partner offers have separate eligibility and redemption requirements. Meanwhile, 7-Eleven is advertising 25 cents off per gallon for three fill-ups through a promotional text offer. Customers can text SAVE to 711711 to access the advertised promotion . Its 7Rewards program also advertises an introductory offer of 11 cents per gallon on the first seven qualifying fill-ups or during the first 90 days, whichever comes first. After the introductory period, members can receive at least five cents off per gallon at eligible stations. The introductory promotions are especially relevant for drivers who haven’t already enrolled in the companies’ respective loyalty programs. Walmart and Amazon members can also save on gasoline Gasoline discounts are no longer limited to companies that primarily sell fuel. Walmart+ members can save 10 cents per gallon at participating Walmart, CITGO, Exxon, Mobil and Murphy fuel stations, and receive member fuel prices at Sam’s Club. Unlike free loyalty programs, Walmart+ ordinarily requires a paid membership, although some customers qualify for discounted subscriptions. Amazon Prime members can also receive 10 cents off per gallon through BP’s Earnify program after linking their accounts. The discount combines Earnify’s regular five-cent-per-gallon benefit with an additional five-cent Prime benefit. For drivers who already pay for these subscriptions, the rewards can provide additional savings without purchasing a separate fuel membership. Love’s Travel Stops also advertises 10 cents off each gallon of gasoline and up to 25 cents off auto diesel through its rewards app, although the offer is excluded at certain locations. Exxon and Mobil, meanwhile, allow Rewards+ members to earn three points per gallon of regular gasoline or six points per gallon of premium fuel. These points can be redeemed for future savings rather than automatically applied as discounts at every fill-up. The differences between these programs can be substantial. A 25-cent-per-gallon discount saves $3.75 on a 15-gallon purchase, while a $1-per-gallon reward saves $15. However, drivers should also compare the actual posted prices at nearby stations. A larger loyalty discount doesn’t necessarily mean the final price will be lower than at a competing gas station. With Thanksgiving travel underway, the savings could be meaningful for households planning several fill-ups over the holiday weekend. title: Target cut its Apple Black Friday discount in half
summary: There are two Target rules customers should know before buying.
content: Target is promoting its 2026 Black Friday event as an expanded eight-day sale, but shoppers looking for major discounts on flagship electronics will notice smaller price cuts than last year. The Minneapolis-based retail giant launched its main Black Friday sale on Sunday, Nov. 22, running through Sunday, Nov. 29. That schedule adds one extra day compared with its seven-day event in 2025. Behind the broader promotion, however, Target scaled back the headline ceiling on some of its most-searched holiday tech items. Target cuts Apple Black Friday savings in half In its official holiday announcement , Target said shoppers can save “up to $100 on select Apple devices” during its Black Friday event. That is half the maximum discount Target advertised during Black Friday 2025, when Apple savings topped out at $200 off select products, according to an analysis by Digital Citizen and Target’s official 2025 holiday announcement . Target’s current sale includes markdowns on specific Apple device and accessories: Apple AirPods Pro 3: Marked down to $149.99 from $249.99 , a $100 discount. Apple Watch Series 12 (42mm GPS): Reduced to $299.99 from $399.99 , also hitting the $100 ceiling. 11-inch Apple iPad (A16, 128GB): Discounted by $70 to $379.99 . Source: Target’s Weekly Ad (with price reported on the morning of November 26) At the same time, a major gaming discount vanished from Target’s Black Friday lineup. Last year, the retailer advertised a flat $100 off PlayStation 5 consoles. Target cut its Apple Black Friday discount in half. Bloomberg / Getty Images In 2026, Target’s Black Friday announcement omitted PlayStation consoles entirely, highlighting gaming deals on Nintendo, Nex, and Meta Quest instead. While Target discounted DualSense PS5 controllers by $20 to $64.99, console buyers will not find last year’s $100 markdown. There is one quiet exception in Target’s live Black Friday lineup. Despite advertising a $100 ceiling in its press release, Target discounted Apple AirPods Max 2 by $120, dropping the over-ear headphones to $429.99 from $549.99, according to Target’s product listing , though Amazon and Best Buy still undercut that price by $10, per NBC News Select . Why Target is holding back on deep tech markdowns Target enters the 2026 holiday weekend in a much stronger financial position than it held a year ago. In its third-quarter earnings report released Nov. 18, Target posted a 7.1% jump in net sales and a 5.6% increase in comparable sales, according to Target’s Q3 2026 financial release . Customer traffic rose 5% year over year, reversing a 2.2% traffic decline during the same quarter in 2025. Because shoppers are already returning to Target stores and digital channels, the chain raised its full-year sales outlook. Jefferies analysts said in a note this month that Target’s recent price cuts and focus on newness have been bringing customers back, according to Retail Dive . That momentum may leave Target with less need for aggressive loss-leader console or Apple discounts to get customers through the door. Across retail, many companies are also holding leaner inventories after tariff disruptions to protect margins, which leaves less excess stock to clear at deep discounts, University of Miami professor Claudia Townsend told NBC News Select . Instead, Target is spreading promotional dollars across mass-traffic giveaways and everyday categories. On Black Friday morning, Nov. 27, stores open at 6 a.m. local time and will hand out gift cards worth $25, $50, or $100 to the first 100 shoppers in line, including one $1,000 gift card per store, according to Target’s Black Friday press release . Meanwhile, competitors are still using higher Apple ceilings to pull tech shoppers away. Best Buy launched its Black Friday sale on Nov. 19 with up to $250 off select MacBook Air models, while Amazon also advertised discounts exceeding $100 on higher-end Apple hardware. Knowing where rivals beat Target is only half the equation; shoppers also need to watch how consumer buying habits are shifting this week and check two strict Target rules before buying. Related: Shoppers ditch Hostess snack cakes while Uncrustables sell faster than factories can make them Shoppers are using Black Friday differently in 2026 Even when retailers trim headline tech discounts, Americans are still planning to spend heavily over Thanksgiving weekend, though what they put in their carts is changing. Nearly two-thirds of U.S. consumers, or 64%, say they are likely to wait until Thanksgiving weekend to do most of their holiday shopping, up from 51% five years ago, according to the National Retail Federation . Overall holiday retail sales are projected to grow 4.2% to $1.013 trillion. At the same time, budget-conscious households are using Cyber Week sales to stock up on everyday necessities alongside gifts. Online sales of personal hygiene products are projected to jump 150% during Cyber Week, compared with September levels, as shoppers hunt for deals on clothing basics, household cleaning supplies, and daily essentials, according to Adobe’s 2026 Holiday Shopping Report . That shift plays directly into Target’s core strengths in apparel, beauty, and household goods, where the retailer is still offering up to 50% off apparel and accessories, 40% off beauty and health gift sets, and 50% off decorative pillows and throws during its Nov. 26–29 weekend wave. Two Target rules shoppers should know before purchasing If you still plan to buy electronics at Target this weekend, whether for convenience or to stack an extra 5% discount with a Target Circle Card, pay close attention to two policies that can save or cost you money: Use the Holiday Price Match Guarantee: Any eligible item purchased at Target between Nov. 1 and Dec. 24 qualifies for a price adjustment if Target lowers its own price later in the season, TheStreet previously reported . Keep your receipt or Circle account record in case Cyber Monday or December flash deals drop prices further. Watch the shorter Apple return clock: Target gives most electronics and entertainment purchases a generous return window starting Dec. 26. However, Apple and Beats products, along with unlocked or prepaid phones, have only a 14-day holiday return window, meaning items bought for Christmas must be returned by Jan. 8, 2027, rather than Jan. 24 for standard electronics, as noted by Digital Citizen . Checking competitor prices on big-ticket Apple devices and noting that early January deadlines can help shoppers avoid overpaying, or getting stuck with an unreturnable gift, during the busiest shopping weekend of the year. title: Black Friday’s New Reality: Why Shoppers Are Stocking Up Instead of Splurging
summary: Kelly Goldsmith explores why Black Friday shoppers are prioritizing essentials, value, and smarter spending over holiday splurges.
content: Kelly Goldsmith, PhD. of Vanderbilt University discusses why Black Friday shoppers are focusing more on everyday essentials and value-driven purchases. Learn how economic uncertainty, personalized marketing, and smart shopping strategies are reshaping the holiday retail season. Jeffrey Snyder, Broadcast Retirement Network Well, Dr. Goldsmith, it’s a pleasure to see you. Thank you so much for joining us, and especially post-Thanksgiving on Black Friday. Kelly Goldsmith, PhD., Vanderbilt University Yes, well, it’s my sincere pleasure. Black Friday is one of my very favorite things to talk about. Jeffrey Snyder, Broadcast Retirement Network Okay, so why is that? Do you enjoy shopping? Do you enjoy observing shopping? Is that part of your day-to-day life as someone at Vanderbilt? Kelly Goldsmith, PhD., Vanderbilt University Yeah, I mean, for the past 22 years, I’ve been in the field of behavioral marketing, which is really all about understanding consumer decision-making and the psychological factors that are at play when we go to the cash register. And I think within marketing, Black Friday, it’s a mainstay in the marketer’s toolkit, as we all know from our inboxes this time of year. Jeffrey Snyder, Broadcast Retirement Network Yeah, I’ve been getting blasted through Amazon and all the big brands, Target. They want to sell me everything under the sun. Let me ask you, take a step back. Affordability has been a big challenge here in the United States, as around the world. How is that, in your mind, as a professor of marketing and someone who runs a department and someone who has been in this industry for a long time, how does that shape or color this year’s Black Friday? Kelly Goldsmith, PhD., Vanderbilt University Well, I think always there’s a price-sensitive segment, and the size of the price-sensitive segment can vary based on your product category. So maybe inherently we’re all more price-sensitive when we think about utilitarian goods, for example. But it also can vary based on macroeconomic factors, like if there is a recession or discussion about inflation, that price-sensitive segment will just grow broadly. And I think even post-pandemic, a lot of us, due to real or perceived uncertainty in macroeconomic factors, people have been a little bit more price-sensitive in general. And then those of us who are a little more price-sensitive, when you’re bombarded with marketing messages that cater to more of a price-sensitive audience, like we see on Black Friday, when you’re bombarded by these messages about deals, then it can be really tempting to just click add to cart. But I think there’s a lot of reasons to be a cautious shopper this time of year. Jeffrey Snyder, Broadcast Retirement Network Yeah, I certainly think so. I know GTA, Grand Theft, I’m not a gamer, but I know Grand Theft. Kelly Goldsmith, PhD., Vanderbilt University It’s a big deal. Jeffrey Snyder, Broadcast Retirement Network I have not. That’s a big deal. I wonder, given what you just mentioned, affordability, those games seem to be fairly expensive, but they’re very popular. Are people putting aside the TVs? Do you believe, because we don’t know, will people put aside the TVs and the video game boxes, et cetera, and maybe go more towards, I don’t know, basic gifts and products? Kelly Goldsmith, PhD., Vanderbilt University So you are asking me at the wrong time of year. Usually, I’m a little bit better about having my finger on the pulse of, sorry, my screen just went blurry. I’m a little bit better about having my finger on the pulse of macroeconomic trends. I will say, vis-a-vis the past, let’s say post-pandemic, let’s say since 2023, I do feel like the temperature has gone down a little bit with respect to people’s concern about pricing. That said, there’s still plenty of concerns and uncertainty around things like, is AI going to take jobs or take my job? Will we see inflation? I know the discussion about that does seem to have kind of cooled a little bit this season. But again, I do think, broadly speaking, post-pandemic, we’re dealing with consumers who consider uncertainty and therefore become a little bit more price sensitive, more so than we did when we had that nice 10-year run of the longest bull market in the history of the United States, for sure. Jeffrey Snyder, Broadcast Retirement Network Let me ask you about small businesses, and I mean, not as an economist, but do they have an advantage maybe in this type of environment or less of an advantage versus, say, a big box store like a Walmart, a Target? And will consumers do believe, based on previous experience, that consumers will recognize, hey, it’s a rising tide lifts all ships and they’ll support smaller businesses over larger, or is it really just about price and good? Kelly Goldsmith, PhD., Vanderbilt University Yeah, I mean, we can all introspect and ask ourselves, when are the times when we really will even maybe pay more to support a small business than just go with what’s available on Amazon, which oftentimes, like an Amazon, a Costco, there’s certain retailers who will pretty reliably have a lower price. And there’s some people who have entirely just kind of cut off their relationship with Amazon for a variety of reasons. And they know that in doing so, it’s either they might be paying a little bit more or there might be more friction with respect to how they acquire their purchases, could be actually going to the store and parking in the parking lot as opposed to getting a bunch of packages from Prime right on your porch. So I think the extent to which we shift our buying to more kind of local mom and pop stores really depends on the person. It depends on the product category. Certainly, like during the pandemic, looking back, we did see a lot of people shift their dollars to what we call personalized sellers. And these could be Etsy stores or places where you feel like you’re supporting another human being. Like shopping on Amazon doesn’t give us as much the sensation that we’re supporting another human being, the way we would get that sensation if we shop in an Etsy store. And so we did see more purchases track in that direction, in part because during the pandemic, a lot of us were experiencing a sense of social isolation. So those kinds of connections felt important and it felt important to support others. I think today, again, it depends on the product category. There’s always going to be things for which we just want to get the lowest price. This is why those deal aggregators exist online and are so successful, because they’re out there trolling the whole World Wide Web to find, you know, where can you get a Dyson vacuum at the cheapest price on Black Friday? There’s always people that are going to be interested in that. Jeffrey Snyder, Broadcast Retirement Network How much does personalization play a role? You mentioned social media, or I’m mentioning social media, but you talked about these aggregators. What Jeff Snyder wants is going to be different than Dr. Goldsmith or my wife or my mom, dad, brother, loved one, whomever out there. How much is that playing a role this year versus, or will that play a role this year versus maybe previous years, or has it only become more enhanced? Kelly Goldsmith, PhD., Vanderbilt University Well, I think it’s social media. Like from a marketing standpoint, one can view the targeted ads are able to do on social media. It’s kind of amazing, because that’s why when you scroll through your Instagram feed, the ads are all really tempting, because they are idiosyncratically customized based on what they know you want. Like we, at least me, my experience, like I don’t tend to get ads for things that aren’t relevant to me anymore, the way that we used to. When targeted ads, I mean, in the not too distant past, used to be a much more blunt instrument where they’d say, okay, women age 34 to 54, they would all like low-fat yogurt, right? Like it’s much more nuanced these days, and that’s why there’s so much harder to resist. And so I think to the extent that technology has continued to improve, and those targeted ads have continued to become more customized just for us, they become harder to resist. And of course, you layer on top of that, the increased prevalence of AI and reliance on AI in analyzing patterns and developing those niche messages that really know how to reach into our hearts and minds. It’s hard as a consumer to be vigilant about not adding to cart every time we see something in our feed. Jeffrey Snyder, Broadcast Retirement Network So to that point, I was going to ask you about artificial intelligence, because I can understand it crafting the message, but is it so sophisticated enough that they can actually create an ad specific to Jeffrey Snyder’s cookies and cash and web usage? So can it, based on the subject matter, but actually create something from scratch? For me, that would be different from you. Kelly Goldsmith, PhD., Vanderbilt University Yeah, I mean, certainly AI, when you think about it on a much smaller scale, we can think about business-to-business marketing, where maybe you’ve only got 10 clients, but you’re running a multimillion-dollar company because those 10 clients really give you a lot of revenue, right? So in those contexts, you could certainly leverage AI to develop, like think about having it write your emails, think about having it do your communication strategy. Like AI can be very helpful in executing an end-to-end marketing plan when you’re dealing with a small customer base for whom you have a lot of information, as would be the case in like a B2B situation. In a broader B2C strategy, where you might, like if you’re Procter & Gamble or Nestle, you might have hundreds of millions of customers who come through your brands. It’s not that it’s impossible to do that really individual-level customization. It’s just that it’s a lot more time-intensive and it costs a lot more money. So these brands have to ask themselves, at what point is the juice worth the squeeze? So I think really where we’ll start to see AI have a bigger influence is when people have smaller customer bases that they can know really, really well, and there’s a high return on investment from customizing your messages. And then over time, who’s to say, right? As AI becomes cheaper and easier to use for a broader base of brands and firms, it’s very possible we could end up in a universe where there’s uniquely customized ads just for us. Jeffrey Snyder, Broadcast Retirement Network We’ve got a couple of minutes left and I want to ask you about gamification. We’ve seen a lot of success of using that with like the sports betting prediction marketing, or excuse me, prediction market apps. How does gamification, I would think it’s kind of analogous to what we were just talking about. You make it into a game or somehow it secretes serotonin in your brain. It’s more apt to have you pull the trigger. Are those tactics that have been successful in sports betting, as an example, come through to the marketing done by Target and Walmart and even smaller businesses? Kelly Goldsmith, PhD., Vanderbilt University Sure. I mean, I think we’ve actually seen versions of gamification in marketing before the word gamification existed. So for example, like you think about, I believe they’re running this promotion right now. And if they’re not, they ran it really recently, the McDonald’s Monopoly game, which has existed at least since I was a child. Jeffrey Snyder, Broadcast Retirement Network Yeah, for at least 40 years. Kelly Goldsmith, PhD., Vanderbilt University Yeah, exactly, right? So that is a form of gamification where you don’t know what you’re going to get when you pull off the tab on your soda. And it might be a point that you have to collect all these points and then you can redeem it, or it might be a car, right? Like that is a form of gamification that people can get very excited by in everyday consumer purchases. And I think there’s other ways, really going back to Black Friday, for some of us, it is gamifying marketing. It’s not that you just get an email from one of your favorite brands and it tells you everything’s 30% off and you get excited. For a lot of customers, and we have collected data that supports this, that email sets off a trigger where you start challenging yourself on how you can find the best deal. Like, okay, I know I’ve got 30% off if I go to this website. Well, what if I go to this website that also often carries the same products? Well, what if instead of going to Nordstrom, I go to Nordstrom Rack? Well, it turns out they both have the same T-shirt, but they’re different prices. So then you start getting into this game across retailers where you’re trying to find the best price, which it’s not a game everybody wants to play. But for a lot of people, almost independent of wealth levels, it can feel pretty fun. And it does make you feel like you’re walking away with the best deal because you engage in like this hand-to-hand combat against these firms. So I will say from the firm side, it actually is not what firms wanna see you do. Which is partly why our research, I think, was a little bit informative to firms. Because what we showed is these deal messages can actually trigger the psychology where rather than hitting add to cart on their website, maybe you keep that browser open and look at like five more websites. And usually you wanna keep the customer there. And so that can be a real challenge in online retail where our mobile or whatever you wanna call it, where it’s so costless to search across retailers. Jeffrey Snyder, Broadcast Retirement Network Yeah. Last question. I promise I’ll let you go back to your office and doing what you like to do. Are there ways… Fraud is a big deal. Mixed messages. I think about cryptocurrency as an example or AMC and GameStop. I’m sure you read or been involved in research about that. How do you counter in today’s environment, if you’re a consumer, you wanna make sure that they’re gamifying, they meaning the marketers are gamifying things, they’re making it attractive, they’re secreting through their efforts, they’re secreting the serotonin and the other neurotransmitters to make it feel right. How do you prevent yourself from falling into that fraud or scam or bad buying trap? Kelly Goldsmith, PhD., Vanderbilt University Okay. I could be naive here, but I like to think we have a very… There’s lots of different ways to litigate against firms if you feel like they’re actually engaged in fraud and people certainly do. So I think any well-managed brands or firms, like brands or firms you’re familiar with are probably operating within the law. So therefore it’s not actually… Again, I could be naive, but I don’t think it’s most firms most of the time because it would be showing up. I mean, we all know in this day and age of cancel culture, there’s a lot of amplification when brands do engage in actual deceptive marketing and fraud. I don’t think that’s what most firms do most of the time. That said, they can have marketing tactics and Black Friday is one of them that are so good, right? For many of us, it becomes hard to avoid. That doesn’t make it fraud, that doesn’t make it deceptive, but that does make it a challenge if you’re a consumer who’s susceptible to these messages, how do you keep yourself from overspending? And I think really there’s an entire cottage industry that has developed around that, like some amazing books are out there on financial literacy and really understanding your own budgets and your own constraints. I think that’s often the best you can do. And this is what I tell people about Black Friday. Like, it’s not a good deal if you don’t need it. So certainly hold yourself… The best thing you can do is hold yourself accountable. If you’re walking into Walmart, Target, these places that run massive Black Friday sales, you have to walk in with a list because if you walk out with a new toaster oven that you didn’t need, you just wasted several hundred dollars, right? Even if it was a good deal vis-a-vis average toaster ovens. So I think that’s really the challenge is putting the burden on yourself to hold yourself accountable to your spending. Jeffrey Snyder, Broadcast Retirement Network Yeah, and I don’t think you’re being naive. I think that if you are… And I really wasn’t directing my question towards those big box stores and maybe I asked the question incorrectly because I think if you have bad practices, you will get caught. Kelly Goldsmith, PhD., Vanderbilt University Yeah. Jeffrey Snyder, Broadcast Retirement Network And they will take you. I mean, you look at some of the… I’m not gonna name the brands because some of that stuff is politically motivated. But I guess more bad actors online. And I’m thinking about third parties like state-sponsored or non-state-sponsored. They’re just out there promoting disinformation, disinformation. Are there ways to kind of… And maybe that’s for another conversation. Kelly Goldsmith, PhD., Vanderbilt University That may be for another conversation because that doesn’t feel like a marketing question. Jeffrey Snyder, Broadcast Retirement Network Okay, okay. We’ll leave it there. Kelly Goldsmith, PhD., Vanderbilt University Okay. Jeffrey Snyder, Broadcast Retirement Network Well, Dr. Kelly Goldsmith, thank you so much for joining us. We appreciate it. And look, we look forward to having you back on the program very soon. Happy holidays to you. Kelly Goldsmith, PhD., Vanderbilt University Yes, you too. Thank you.

title: New $799 smart glasses challenge Apple, but with a major catch
summary: A startup promises Vision Pro-style controls in ordinary-looking glasses.
content: Apple spent years creating the Vision Pro headset to change computer interaction. A 45-gram device from a little-known tech startup now promises some of the same interactions. There is a noticeable price difference. After a $200 price hike in June, Apple’s Vision Pro now retails for $3,699. The price of the recently revealed Orrorin Glasses is anticipated to be $799. MacRumors reported on Nov. 25, that Hong Kong-based Savage Technology has unveiled smart glasses featuring full-color displays for both eyes and gesture controls inspired by Apple’s Vision Pro. Savage’s glasses are designed to appear like traditional eyeglasses, in contrast to Apple’s headgear, which needs much more technology. Users reportedly don’t need a separate controller or wristband to browse digital information with tiny finger motions. As Apple, Meta Platforms (META) , and other businesses compete to define the next wave of wearable technology, this development is emerging. However, there’s a crucial catch. Though the first shipments of Orrorin are planned for 2027, it is still an incomplete product. The glasses also lack several features that enable Apple’s spatial computing experience, despite their similarity to Vision Pro. That presents a compelling issue for consumers: Would more affordable, less complicated glasses be more useful than a pricey mixed-reality headset? New $799 Orrorin glasses promise to rival Apple’s Vision Pro controls Savage Technology, founded by Bill Pei and Elena Shi, says its Orrorin Glasses combine miniature displays, eye tracking, and gesture recognition. In addition to claiming a weight advantage of almost 25 times when Apple’s external battery is added, the business characterizes the gadget as providing interactions similar to those seen on Vision Pro. According to Savage’s official product specifications, the glasses feature: Weight: 45 grams Price: $799 Displays: Full-color MicroLED screens for both eyes Resolution: 500 by 380 pixels at 60Hz Brightness: Up to 1,800 nits Battery: Up to 10 hours of claimed usage Storage: 4GB Controls: Finger gestures and eye tracking The company’s central innovation is its proposed interaction system. Without the need for other attachments, users can interact with digital information by making tiny pinching gestures. When users look away, eye tracking enables the displays to automatically dim. Savage also plans to use teleprompters, messaging, sports information, and navigation. SavageOS allows developers to construct programs, including tools made using coding helpers, including Codex and Claude Code. But since they haven’t been objectively confirmed in a shipping consumer product, such capabilities are still promises. Apple’s Vision Pro offers something the new Orrorin glasses cannot Spatial computing is the primary distinction between the companies’ glasses. Apple Vision Pro allows digital windows and objects to look rooted in real-world locations by tracking the user’s position and surroundings. Savage’s glasses lack the positioning tracking and spatial mapping necessary to provide that experience. As a result, Orrorin cannot replicate the full immersive capabilities of Apple’s headset. MacRumors noted Nov. 25 that the glasses are designed for simpler interactions and are not intended to replace Vision Pro’s broader computing capabilities. In addition, Apple’s smartphone has strong processing capabilities, high-resolution screens, and advanced sensors. The company updated Vision Pro with its M5 chip in October 2025, improving performance while retaining its external battery design. The difference is noteworthy for customers. In the future, Orrorin could appeal to those who want lightweight digital help and alerts without wearing a heavy headset. On the other hand, Vision Pro fulfills a new function by providing spatial computing, productivity, and immersive entertainment. Although the devices may share certain controls, they are not comparable products. Apple and Meta face a surprising new $799 competitor. Mario Tama / Getty Images Meta’s $799 smart glasses face a new competitor Instead of Apple, Meta may be Savage’s primary rival. In September 2025, Meta launched its Ray-Ban Display spectacles, which start at $799. The device has a Neural Band wristband that translates muscle impulses into instructions and a full-color display. Meta says users can interact with messages, navigation information, and other features without constantly reaching for a smartphone. The suggested benefit of Orrorin is that it inserts displays in both eyes and does away with the need for a separate bracelet. One display is placed in the right eye of the Meta Ray-Ban Display. Nonetheless, Meta already has a well-known consumer product, retail distribution, and expertise in producing smart eyewear. Savage, on the other hand, is trying to launch its first product. That difference may end up being more significant than the requirements. The biggest catch is the 2027 Orrorin release date Savage Technology says its Orrorin Glasses are still undergoing engineering validation. Reservations are being accepted; however, buyers are not currently able to order a completed gadget for prompt delivery. Its published schedule calls for: Founder Edition: $199 deposit, estimated shipping in March 2027 Early Bird: $29 deposit, estimated shipping in May 2027 In Line: $49 deposit, estimated shipping in July 2027 All deposits count toward the $799 purchase price. The company’s terms make clear that these are estimated shipping dates, not guaranteed delivery commitments. According to reports, Apple is getting ready to release its smart glasses in 2027. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has reported that Apple’s initial model is expected to emphasize cameras, microphones, speakers, and Siri integration rather than built-in displays. The market for wearable AI gadgets may become more competitive as a result. The more general issue for investors in Apple (AAPL) and Meta is which businesses can transform smart glasses into something that people want to wear all day. Savage’s statement serves as an example of how smaller businesses are experimenting with headset substitutes. However, its lofty requirements, unknown technology, and unclear delivery timetable continue to be major challenges. As of now, Orrorin is more of an interesting promise than a proven substitute for Vision Pro. And making smart glasses comfortable, reasonably priced, and genuinely helpful may be more important for the industry’s next breakthrough than producing the most advanced technology. title: Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy protection, passengers left stranded
summary: The airline canceled all flights operations on November 26.
content: Norse Atlantic Airways, a Norwegian low-cost airline that at one point flew to five cities in the U.S., has filed for bankruptcy and canceled all flights as the latest in a long string of budget airline collapses. “The Board of Norse Atlantic Airways AS has made the difficult decision to file for bankruptcy despite extensive efforts from the Company and the Group to find a solution,” Norse Chief Executive Eivind Roald wrote in a Nov. 27 statement. “We are deeply sorry for the impact this has on our passengers, employees and partners.” Two days earlier, the carrier forebodingly canceled two flights that it was scheduled to operate for Pakistan International Airlines through a wet lease as well as another route between London Gatwick and Orlando originally slated to run on Nov. 26. Norse Atlantic shuts down, tells passengers with flights to “not go to the airport” Any additional flights that Norse was scheduled to run to cities like Cape Town, Bangkok and Phuket from London and Scandinavian cities like Oslo and Stockholm in the coming weeks have now also been canceled. In a large pop-up that comes up for anyone going on the Norse website, customers are told “not go to the airport for a cancelled flight” because the company is “going into an insolvency process” at the Agder District Court in northern Norway. The shutdown also includes any return flights that were booked part of one ticket as well as the airline’s cargo branch that transported goods to different corners of Europe. Related: Low-cost airline Norse Atlantic cancels flights, appears to shut down This collapse could leave hundreds of travelers stranded in the coming days. Those who need to fly out are being advised to book with another airline. As prices in such situations tend to spike, competitor airlines may end up offering rescue flights with lowered fares in the days to come. “If you still need to travel, look for a flight with another airline,” Norse writes further. “If you have travel insurance, ask your insurer whether it covers airline failure or the cost of getting home before buying a replacement ticket, if possible.” Norse Atlantic Airways began operations in 2022 as a transatlantic budget airline. Mrkit99 / Getty Images What to do if you booked with Norse: Alternative flights and refund options Given its financial collapse, Norse will be unable to compensate travelers with canceled flights. The fastest way to get a refund is to go through the credit card one used to purchase the ticket or the travel insurance one bought to protect the trip. Those without either option will need to through the insolvency process through the Norwegian government. Fly Beena’s plans were initially announced in April through an early investment from the conglomerate. Global Airlines: The airline startup, launched by holiday travel platform Holiday Swap founder James Asquith, was shut down when the High Court of Justice in London issued a winding-up petition on Nov. 4 . title: Thanksgiving airfares jumped 57% as a new travel risk emerges
summary: Americans are paying sharply higher airfares, but recent airline disruptions are giving some travelers another reason to stay off planes.
content: Rising ticket prices have made Thanksgiving travel more expensive for millions of Americans, but some families are reconsidering their holiday flights for other reasons. Driving has become a more appealing option due to a number of flight problems, especially for passengers on trips that might take longer than ten hours. Reuters reported Wednesday, Nov. 25, that domestic Thanksgiving airfares averaged approximately $469 two weeks before the holiday, a 57% increase from the comparable period last year, according to travel search engine Kayak. The significant increase coincides with rising fuel prices, concerns about flight reliability, and a strong Thanksgiving storm for airlines. The Federal Aviation Administration’s nationwide ground stop on Nov. 13, triggered by a technical failure, added to those concerns, disrupting air travel across the country. For some travelers, the convenience of flying is now outweighed by the possibility of another setback. However, Americans are hardly giving up on traveling for Thanksgiving. Just under the previous year’s record of 81.6 million, AAA predicts that 81.5 million people will travel at least 50 miles from home during the holiday season. The travel sector faces a glaring contradiction as a result. Although Americans are becoming more conscious of the cost and dependability of travel, they still wish to see friends and family. The problem for airlines goes beyond just selling pricey tickets. They have to convince passengers that flying is still worth the extra cost and risk. Thanksgiving airfares hit their highest levels in a decade The cost of air travel has become a significant barrier for families planning vacations. Thanksgiving and Christmas fares are at their highest levels in ten years, according to Reuters, partially due to rising jet fuel prices. Although its numbers differ from Kayak’s, AAA’s independent study confirms the pressure. Travelers paid an average of $800 for domestic round-trip Thanksgiving tickets, up 17% from 2025, according to AAA’s Nov. 16 projection. The difference matters. Kayak’s 57% increase measures fares advertised at a particular point before Thanksgiving, while AAA’s 17% increase reflects tickets travelers had already booked. The figures are not directly comparable. Fuel prices are another issue that airlines must deal with. Industry group Airlines for America said jet fuel prices averaged $4.64 per gallon in October, setting a record. Carriers have responded by reducing some flight frequencies, retiring older aircraft, and increasing certain fees. Higher ticket costs are particularly upsetting to customers when multiple family members need to travel together. FAA’s nationwide disruption adds another warning Ticket prices are just one issue. Flights were halted nationwide Nov. 13 after a technical failure destabilized air traffic communications systems. The disruption started around 3:30 p.m., the agency said. Eastern and normal air traffic resumed at 8:15 p.m. The FAA reported 12,462 flight cancellations that day, but not all were due to the ground stop. In the days that followed, United Airlines (UAL) and Delta Air Lines (DAL) experienced more technical issues. Related: Target, Kohl’s and JCPenney use Black Friday freebies to lure shoppers Just before the Thanksgiving rush, the interruptions exacerbated worries about aircraft reliability. Another issue arose on Thursday due to severe weather. The Washington Post reported that, as of 12:45 p.m. Eastern on Nov. 26, FlightAware recorded 399 cancellations and 1,336 delays involving flights within, into, or out of the United States. The combination of higher prices, technical disruptions and dangerous weather has made travelers increasingly cautious. Thanksgiving airfares jump 57%, but a bigger problem looms TIMOTHY A. CLARY / Getty Images Millions of Americans are choosing another way to travel AAA’s forecast reveals how Americans are adjusting their Thanksgiving travel plans. The organization projects the following figures for Nov. 24 through Nov. 30: 72.9 million Americans traveling by car, down from 73.1 million last year. 5.96 million traveling by domestic air, a 0.2% decline. 2.6 million using buses, trains and cruises, an increase of 4.1%. 81.5 million total travelers, compared with 81.6 million in 2025. For nearly 90% of Thanksgiving travelers, driving remains their top choice. Road excursions are not exempt from rising expenses due to rising gas prices. Interest is also growing in other transit providers. On the day of the FAA interruption, bookings on travel platform Wanderu increased by almost 16%, while bus operator Flix North America reported a 17% spike in Thanksgiving reservations, according to a Reuters story on Wednesday. Amtrak, meanwhile, expects another strong Thanksgiving season after recording 1.2 million passenger trips during the holiday period last year. These changes suggest that passengers are seeking alternatives, even though overall AAA statistics do not show a national increase in driving compared with the previous year. What the Thanksgiving travel shift means for airlines Major US carriers must perform a challenging balancing act amid an evolving travel landscape. Airlines for America expects approximately 29 million passengers between Nov. 20 and Nov. 30. American Airlines (AAL) expects over 8 million passengers, while United expects over 6.6 million during its Thanksgiving travel period. Airlines have planned more capacity despite worries about demand. Flight analytics company Cirium estimates that US carriers are operating approximately 2% more flights than last Thanksgiving, with seat capacity increasing 1%, Reuters reported. Turning such capacity into profitable travel while controlling fuel prices and operational disruptions is the airlines’ problem. Price-conscious consumers may be turned off by higher ticket prices, even though they might help offset costs. Travelers are making decisions that go beyond simply comparing tickets. Reliability, overall costs, and the possibility of missing Thanksgiving festivities are now major factors. Although there is still strong demand for vacation travel, the industry’s most recent data show a significant shift. Americans are still committed to getting where they want to go. When it comes to how much they pay and how they get there, they are becoming more picky. Related: Black Friday shoppers face a surprising AI pricing twist
